<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hellknight-Errant](/Feats.aspx?ID=8817) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 25

**Archetype** [Hellknight](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=372)

**Prerequisites**
[Hellknight Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8812); you've refused to take or have failed the Hellknight Test.

</column>

---

Either through unfortunate circumstances or your own choice, you remain a Hellknight armiger instead of entering the true ranks of your order, though you still believe in the tenets of law and order. You likely take on an adventuring life with a group of like-minded individuals who aren't Hellknights. The resistance to mental damage you gained from the Hellknight Dedication feat increases to 5 + your number of archetype class feats from the Hellknight archetype.

 You also gain the Warding Shift action, which allows you to keep your allies from harm.

 **Warding Shift** <actions string="Single Action" /> **Requirements** You're adjacent to a willing ally; **Effect** You move the adjacent willing ally 5 feet in any direction and can Step into the space the ally vacated.

**Special** You can't take both this feat and [Hellknight Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8818) or [Hellknight Signifer Preferment](/Feats.aspx?ID=8819).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hellspawn](/Feats.aspx?ID=1381) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Lineage" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=317" />
<trait label="Tiefling" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=258" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 40

</column>

---

Your lineage descends from [devils](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=30), the conniving schemers of [Hell's](/Planes.aspx?ID=18) malevolent hierarchy. You're as skilled at noticing lies and twisted wordings as you are at constructing them. You are trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) and [Legal Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8). If you were already trained in Deception (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You also gain the [Lie to Me](/Feats.aspx?ID=811) skill feat.

<title level="2">Hellspawn leads to...</title>

    level="1"
    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Helpful Halfling](/Feats.aspx?ID=1021) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Halfling" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=87" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 45

</column>

---

When you aid a friend with a task, you find many ways to help and avoid interfering. On a critical success to [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75), you grant your ally a +3 circumstance bonus if you have expert proficiency in the skill (rather than +2), and you grant your ally a +4 circumstance bonus if you have master proficiency (rather than +3). If you roll a critical failure on a check to Aid, you don’t give your ally a –1 circumstance penalty to their check.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Helt's Spelldance](/Feats.aspx?ID=4130) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Bard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=19" />
<trait label="Sorcerer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=148" />
<trait label="Witch" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=323" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 77

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12)

**Access**
Members of the Firebrands at the rank of second mark or higher have access to this feat.

</column>

---

Ranik Helt knows a special technique to hide his spells as part of a performance, and you've learned this technique. Ostentatiously performing, you move across the battlefield, taking foes aback and creating an opening for your spell. Attempt a Performance check against all observers' Perception DCs. Then, Stride once or twice. During this movement, you don't trigger reactions that are triggered by your movement from the creatures against which you succeeded on your Performance check. After your movement, you can Cast a Spell. If you used one Stride, you can cast either a 1-action or a 2-action spell; if you used two Strides, you can only cast a 1-action spell. If you critically succeed on your check against any creature, they take a –1 circumstance penalty to their saving throws against any spell you cast as part of your Helt's Spelldance due to your distracting performance. All creatures that observed you become temporarily immune to your Helt's Spelldance for 10 minutes.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hematocritical](/Feats.aspx?ID=7244) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Fortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=612" />
<trait label="Rage" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=680" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 61

**Archetype** [Bloodrager](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=283)

**Prerequisites**
[Bloodrager Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7239)

**Requirements**
Your last action was a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) that critically hit a creature that isn’t immune to bleed damage.

</column>

---

You bathe in the arterial fluids of your enemy, drinking deep of their freed essence to empower your magic and increase your spellcasting efficacy. If your next action is to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) that requires a spell attack roll, you roll the spell attack roll twice and use the better result; this is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect. Alternatively, if your next action is to cast a spell that requires the creature damaged by the triggering strike to attempt a save, they roll twice and take the lower result; this is a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Henge Gate](/Feats.aspx?ID=9208) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Runesmith" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=952" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 52

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

</column>

---

You hold a rune in your heart and strike the earth, causing two standing stones to rise nearby, your chosen rune carved upon their surfaces and blazing in the air above them. The stones each appear in an unoccupied 5-foot space within 30 feet of you and within 15 feet of each other. When you raise the henge gate, choose one rune that can be drawn on a creature to carve into the stones. If you or an ally makes a successful ranged [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) using physical ammunition and that attack passes through the henge gate, the ammunition gains that rune in flight and automatically traces it on the target. The henge gate lasts for 1 minute.

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 283 **Archetype** [Mortal Herald](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=305) **Prerequisites** [Herald's Weapon](/Feats.aspx?ID=7532) --- The power of your blows can send your victim hurling through your deity’s realm for a fragment of a second. You activate Herald’s Weapon, ignoring the frequency, and make a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with your transformed weapon or unarmed attack against a creature. If you hit and deal damage, the target must attempt a Will save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. If your Strike was a critical hit, the creature uses the outcome for one degree of success worse than the result of their saving throw. Regardless of the result, the target becomes immune to Herald’s Strike for 10 minutes. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target takes 3d10 [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage and becomes [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 1 round.
**Failure** The target takes 6d10 spirit damage and becomes dazzled for 1 round and [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 1.
**Critical Failure** The target takes 12d10 spirit damage and becomes [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 round and drained 2.

Regardless of the result, the target becomes immune to Herald’s Strike for 10 minutes. Critical Success The target is unaffected. Success The target takes 3d10 spirit damage and becomes dazzled for 1 round. Failure The target takes 6d10 spirit damage and becomes dazzled for 1 round and drained 1. Critical Failure The target takes 12d10 spirit damage and becomes blinded for 1 round and drained 2.

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 176 **Archetype** [Herbalist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=62) **Prerequisites** Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10); [Natural Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=815) --- You can create remedies and other herbal products. You gain the [basic alchemy benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=1435), though they apply only for herbal items: alchemical items with the [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=89) trait, plus [antidote](/Equipment.aspx?ID=80) and [antiplague](/Equipment.aspx?ID=81). You gain batches of infused reagents per day equal to your level or half your level if you didn't make your daily preparations in the wilderness. Your advanced alchemy level for creating these is 1 and doesn't increase on its own. You become an expert in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) and can use Nature instead of [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) herbal items. You don't need to be trained in Crafting or have the [Alchemical Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=752) feat to do so, and you can use [healer's tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=25) instead of [alchemist's tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2). **Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the herbalist archetype. Herbalist Dedication leads to... [Endemic Herbs](/Feats.aspx?ID=1985), [Expert Herbalism](/Feats.aspx?ID=1986), [Fresh Ingredients](/Feats.aspx?ID=1983), [Gravelands Herbalist](/Feats.aspx?ID=3614), [Poultice Preparation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1984) Alchemical Plant Items **Source** [_Lost Omens Travel Guide pg. 12_](https://paizo.com/products/btq02dv8)

You can create natural remedies. You gain the [advanced alchemy benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=3282). You can use advanced alchemy to create 4 [alchemical](/Traits.aspx?ID=528) [consumables](/Traits.aspx?ID=564) with the [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623) trait, though the number is reduced by 2 if you didn’t make your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575) in the wilderness.     right="Feat 6"

>
[Hero-God's Bond](/Feats.aspx?ID=8017) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane
](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 67

**Archetype** [Warrior Of Legend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=286)

**Prerequisites**
[Warrior Of Legend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7261)

</column>

---

At times, the myth of a hero-god includes a favored partner or a bonded ally, such as the hero-gods of promises and shield-bearers, Upion and Warrick. When you gain this feat, select an ally. They are your bonded partner. While you and your bonded partner are on the same plane, you and your bonded partner always have the same [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) value (defaulting to the highest value), so when your bonded partner’s doomed condition would increase or be set to a specific amount, your doomed value also increases to match (if it is lower than your current doomed value). When either of you are dying, the other knows this immediately, as well as the distance and direction to the dying partner’s location. When either of you attempts a [recovery check](/Rules.aspx?ID=2326), as long as the other is on the same plane, reduce the DC of the recovery check by 2. You can communicate telepathically with your bonded partner as long as you are within 60 feet of each other. 

You can change your bonded partner by spending 1 week of downtime bonding with another ally.

<title level="2">Hero-God's Bond leads to...</title>
[Grief's Fury](/Feats.aspx?ID=8019), [Martyr's Parry](/Feats.aspx?ID=8018)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs=""
>
[Heroic Scion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8151) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Revenge of the Runelords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Destiny" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=838" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 77

**Archetype** [Heroic Scion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=339)

</column>

---

Destiny calls, and the soul of a dead hero reincarnates to take up the fight! Either an old enemy resumes their efforts to affect chaos and violence, or a new threat arises and you feel compelled to stand against it. You’ve stood against evil before, and the time is nigh for you to do so once again.

When you select this mythic destiny, work with your GM to determine the best choice for which previous PC or NPC serves as the source of your reincarnation. For the Revenge of the Runelords Adventure Path in particular, any PC who played a role in the Rise of the Runelords, Shattered Star, or Return of the Runelords Adventure Paths makes for a perfect fit—as would any allied NPC who, in your previous campaign, perished before the end.

A heroic scion comes into the world when a nemesis from their old adventures returns. In the case of this campaign, the heroic scion’s nemesis are the ancient runelords of Thassilon. In other campaigns, this nemesis can be a specific individual, a coterie of rivals, or an organization you’re destined to oppose. You instinctively know when your nemesis is active in the world. This knowledge may begin as nightmares or a feeling of inevitable conflict but grows stronger and more specific as you contemplate further. You also know when this entity or group has been fully defeated and ceases to operate at all. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) or [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302) whenever an ally or servant of your nemesis attempts to Lie to you, escape your notice, or Impersonate someone else.

Fate has deemed you incredibly hard to kill. You reduce the DC of [recovery checks](/Rules.aspx?ID=2326) by 1.

Choose one skill that’s not a Lore skill, based on the themes of your reincarnated heroic source. Your GM can help you determine a list of appropriate skills to choose from. When you employ an action using that skill, you may spend a Mythic Point to attempt the associated check at mythic proficiency.

Finally, you gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) feat for a special Lore skill subcategory—Incarnation Lore. This Lore skill allows you to become aware of or recall your past exploits. When you increase your proficiency in Incarnation Lore, you remember more about your previous adventures. Certain heroic scion feats require you to attempt an Incarnation Lore check, such as when you attempt the following activity granted you by this feat. 

<document level="2" id="action-3529" />

<title level="2">Heroic Scion Dedication leads to...</title>
[Avoid Fate's Gaze](/Feats.aspx?ID=8152), [Daunting Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=8158), [Eternal Hero](/Feats.aspx?ID=8165), [I've Been Here Before](/Feats.aspx?ID=8153), [Internal Dialogue](/Feats.aspx?ID=8154), [Let Death Be My Weapon](/Feats.aspx?ID=8159), [Momentary Respite](/Feats.aspx?ID=8160), [My Reputation Precedes Me](/Feats.aspx?ID=8155), [On My Best Day](/Feats.aspx?ID=8162), [Reincarnated Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=8156), [Telling Blow](/Feats.aspx?ID=8163), [To Me!](/Feats.aspx?ID=8164), [To Thine Own Self](/Feats.aspx?ID=8157), [Vigorous Victor](/Feats.aspx?ID=8161)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs=""
>
[Heroic Weakness](/Feats.aspx?ID=8014) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane
](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 65

**Archetype** [Godling](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=293)

**Prerequisites**
[Godling Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7392); [hero-god accomplishment](/Rules.aspx?ID=3489)

</column>

---

As word of your faith spreads, so too does word of your foibles and weaknesses. Where originally these disadvantages may have been myths themselves, or simply manifestations of ill fortune or chance, when you take this feat, one of those weaknesses becomes real. 

Work with your GM to choose your heroic weakness—it must be to a specific damage type and must be associated with a specific condition, both of which must be elements that are going to be significant parts of your story’s future. For example, you could choose for a [weakness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to be [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage caused to you by a follower of a rival god, physical damage from a specific category of weapon, [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage caused by a specific kind of [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722), or [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) damage taken in a certain part of the world or from creatures from that part of the world. The amount of weakness you gain to this damage is equal to twice your level. 

But with this new weakness comes a new source of power, for when your foes would take advantage of your weakness, you can use the pain and humiliation to bolster your own resolve. You gain the following reaction. 

**Makes Me Stronger** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** You take damage from your heroic weakness and are not reduced to fewer than 1 Hit Point by the damage; **Effect** You make a show of powering through your weakness, be it by flexing your muscles, issuing a challenging roar, laughing off the pain, or simply acting as if the damage doesn’t worry you in the slightest. Your spells gain a status bonus to damage against the triggering creature equal to twice their rank; this lasts until the next time you use this reaction. In addition, the creature that damaged you with your heroic weakness must attempt a Will save against your class or spellcasting DC, whichever is higher, to avoid becoming [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1 (frightened 2 on a critical failure).

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 219

**Archetype** [Draconic Acolyte](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=333)

**Prerequisites**
[Draconic Acolyte Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8090)

</column>

---

Your _draconic gift_ is the key to a repository of treasure that only you can access. You create an extradimensional space that can hold up to 100 Bulk worth of objects. The space functions as a [_spacious pouch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3032), but has no Bulk, and can be [Interacted](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) with using only one hand by touching your _draconic gift_. You can normally store and retrieve items that could fit through the opening of a bag (as _spacious pouch_). However, you can store an unattended item larger than would normally fit (but no larger than 10 Bulk) by spending 1 minute concentrating on your _draconic gift_ as you press it against the object. Retrieving it takes 1 minute and causes the item to appear in the closest unoccupied space.

You've learned to hide the magical auras of your gear. During your daily preparations, you carefully tweak any or all of your magic items to appear non-magical. When you [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) a temporary item using Scrounger Dedication, it can be an item of up to 3rd level (though the item must still be a weapon, armor, or a nonconsumable piece of adventuring gear). You can instead Craft it for someone else's use, allowing them to avoid taking the penalty for using a shoddy item when using it, but causing you to take the penalty if you use it.

**Source** [Pathfinder #180: The Smoking Gun](/Sources.aspx?ID=125) pg. 79 **Archetype** [Clockwork Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=184) **Frequency** once per hour **Prerequisites** [Clockwork Reanimator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3645) --- Your clockwork devices can commandeer the bodies of [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), bending them to your will. Make a melee Strike against an adjacent undead creature. On a success, instead of taking damage, the target becomes [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=6) by you if its level is equal to or lower than your level – 3. It can attempt a Will saving throw against the higher of your class DC or spell DC to resist being controlled by you. If the target is already under someone else's command, the controlling creature also rolls a saving throw, and the undead uses the better result. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected and temporarily immune for 24 hours.
**Success** The target is unaffected.
**Failure** The undead creature becomes a [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=109) under your control for 1 minute. The control ends if you or an ally attacks the minion undead.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the duration is 1 hour. Hijack Undead leads to... [Improved Hijack Undead](/Feats.aspx?ID=3651)

[History of Violence](/Feats.aspx?ID=7306) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
<trait label="Void" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=510" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 107

**Archetype** [Apocalypse Rider](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=287)

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Prerequisites**
[Apocalypse Rider Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7304)

</column>

---

Your attacks bring with them echoes of previous battles, calling the unquiet victims of your most brutal acts to savage your opponents. Make a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306). If this Strike hits, you deal additional [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage equal to your key attribute modifier to the target and all enemies within 30 feet. If your attack is a critical hit, you deal twice as much damage instead, and the target of your Strike takes [persistent void damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) equal to your key attribute modifier as your fallen foes attempt to drag the target into oblivion with them. This Strike counts as two attacks for calculating your multiple attack penalty.

>
[Hoarder's Craw](/Feats.aspx?ID=8067) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Kobold" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=224" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 214

**Prerequisites**
[Dragonscaled Kobold](/Heritages.aspx?ID=334) heritage

</column>

---

Your draconic features include a pouch inside your body that you use to store food prior to digestion. However, instead of swallowing rocks or other minerals to help grind your food, you swallow gold and other precious ores for the same purpose. Inside your craw, you can store up to 100 coins (of any type) or an amount of precious material that’s light Bulk (usually a chunk). Items can be concealed inside your craw or regurgitated as an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action. Instead of precious material or coins, you can also use your craw to conceal an item of light Bulk but can only do so for up to 1 hour before you must regurgitate it. While carrying anything other than precious material or coins in your craw, you become [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) 1 due to the discomfort.

The connection between you and the [First World](/Planes.aspx?ID=10) resonates within your body stronger than it does for most gnomes, allowing you to cross the threshold between the [Material Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=1) and the First World. You gain [_plane shift_](/Spells.aspx?ID=222) as a primal innate spell. You can cast it twice per week. This can be used only to travel back and forth between the First World and the Material Plane. Due to your body's natural resonance, you can act as the spell focus, and you don't require a tuning fork.

<traits>

<trait label="Psychic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=430" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 24

</column>

---

As your spell strikes a target, you plant a beacon in the target's mind that announces its presence to those nearby. Use this amp in place of a psi cantrip's normal amp entry. The amped cantrip must be one that has one or more targets and must either require a spell attack roll or have a saving throw.

---
**Amp** Choose one creature hit by the spell (if the spell has a spell attack roll) or that fails its save against the spell (if the spell requires a save). A psychic beacon emits from the creature's location, making it easier to notice the creature as the mind and attention of onlookers is subtly drawn to it. For 1 minute, if the target would be [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26), it's instead merely [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4), and if it would be concealed, it's no longer concealed.

Members of the Firebrands at the rank of second mark or higher have access to this feat.

**Requirements**
A rope is within your reach, or you have a [rope](/Equipment.aspx?ID=44) or [grappling](/Traits.aspx?ID=184) weapon in your hand.

</column>

---

The Salt Breakers learned to use whatever they could during the Vidric Revolution, and they quickly mastered the art of making a rope into a useful tool in combat. You take hold of a nearby rope, throw a rope from your hand, or fire a grappling weapon at a solid surface—and then swing up to twice your Speed. If you end your movement next to an enemy, attempt an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) that enemy, tying them up in your rope.

---

You've internalized the hopping gait of your vampiric forebear. Stride up to a distance equal to your Speed – 10 feet. During this Stride, instead of moving through each space normally, you hop over every other square between your starting space and your ending space. These hops aren't high enough to jump over a creature or other significant obstacle in your way, but they avoid difficult terrain, hazardous terrain, pressure plates, or hazards on the ground or up to a foot above it in the spaces you hopped over.

</column>

---

You've mastered travel within a specific type of terrain. You gain the [Favored Terrain](/Feats.aspx?ID=495) feat. When in your favored terrain, you gain a +10-foot circumstance bonus to your travel Speed. When other creatures [Follow the Expert](/Actions.aspx?ID=514) with you as a guide in your favored terrain, they gain both the ability to ignore non-magical difficult terrain for the purpose of their travel Speed and the bonus to travel Speed.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the horizon walker archetype.

<title level="2">Horizon Walker Dedication leads to...</title>
[Acclimatization](/Feats.aspx?ID=1988), [Magical Adaptation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1991), [Perpetual Scout](/Feats.aspx?ID=1990), [Rebel's Map](/Feats.aspx?ID=4135), [Sure Foot](/Feats.aspx?ID=1989), [Wild Strider](/Feats.aspx?ID=1992)

These effects last until the start of its next turn.

For basic spells, basic movements; you can do without flamboyant gestures or showy signs of power.     pfs="Standard"
>
[Hunter's Defense](/Feats.aspx?ID=2819) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Grippli" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=264" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Mwangi Expanse](/Sources.aspx?ID=89) pg. 120

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10)

**Trigger**
A creature with the [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9), [beast](/Traits.aspx?ID=20), [elemental](/Traits.aspx?ID=57), [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69), [fungus](/Traits.aspx?ID=77), or [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125) trait attacks you, and you can see the attacker. 

</column>

---

Your canny understanding of natural and primal creatures helps you predict and dodge their attacks. The triggering attack roll targets your [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) DC instead of your AC. Though this allows you to avoid taking penalties to your AC, it doesn't remove any conditions or other effects causing such penalties. For example, an enemy with sneak attack would still deal extra damage to you for being [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16), even though you wouldn't take the –2 circumstance penalty against the attack.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Hunter's Sanctum](/Feats.aspx?ID=3476) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 28

**Archetype** [Undead Slayer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=174)

**Prerequisites**
[Undead Slayer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3474)

</column>

---

You establish a safe house where you can prepare for your hunt. The sanctum is roughly the size of a 20-foot cube. This sanctum is in a location you have access to and can be part of a larger structure, such as the basement of a temple or hidden room of a library. Setting up or moving your sanctum takes a week of downtime. Your sanctum protects objects and people inside it from magical detection and the prying eyes of [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160). This has the effects of [_nondetection_](/Spells.aspx?ID=209), using your [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) modifier for the [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC and half your level rounded up for the counteract level. Additionally, undead attempting to locate the entrance to your sanctum via mundane Perception must succeed against either your Religion DC or the normal DC to find the sanctum, whichever is higher.

fields.text: Feat 4 Hunter's Sanctum Archetype Source Book of the Dead pg. 28 Archetype Undead Slayer Prerequisites Undead Slayer Dedication You establish a safe house where you can prepare for your hunt. The sanctum is roughly the size of a 20-foot cube. This sanctum is in a location you have access to and can be part of a larger structure, such as the basement of a temple or hidden room of a library. Setting up or moving your sanctum takes a week of downtime. Your sanctum protects objects and people inside it from magical detection and the prying eyes of undead. This has the effects of nondetection , using your Religion modifier for the counteract DC and half your level rounded up for the counteract level. Additionally, undead attempting to locate the entrance to your sanctum via mundane Perception must succeed against either your Religion DC or the normal DC to find the sanctum, whichever is higher.

---

When you [Change Shape](/Actions.aspx?ID=701), you retain elements of your kitsune form, allowing you to speak in a fox form, use kitsune unarmed attacks in a tailless form, or gain a tail in your tailless form to use abilities that require one. You can Change Shape to alter the details of your hybrid form without fully changing into your true form or your alternate form. While in hybrid form, your foxlike features make it obvious that you aren't a normal humanoid.

>
[Hydra's Bond](/Feats.aspx?ID=8020) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane
](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 68

</column>

---

When the hero-gods built Pol-Sylirica and its seven armies, they feared betrayal from within. They took inspiration from the multi-headed hydra, and bound the seven armies together with supernatural ties to make them behave as if they shared one body. Following these tactics, during [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575), you can select a number of willing creatures equal to half your level to be part of your hydra’s bond. Members of the same hydra’s bond always know if another member is telling the truth. 

When a member of the hydra’s bond saves against an effect that would have them act against their allies (such as the [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) condition, a [_dominate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1501) spell, or other [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects that would give an ally the [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) condition), you can spend a Mythic Point to allow that character to attempt the save at mythic proficiency. If a member of the hydra’s bond fails a save against such an effect, other members automatically know that the target is controlled or under the influence of a mental effect. In addition, all members of the hydra’s bond gain a +2 circumstance bonus to any roll made to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) that effect.

Following these tactics, during daily preparations, you can select a number of willing creatures equal to half your level to be part of your hydra’s bond. Members of the same hydra’s bond always know if another member is telling the truth. When a member of the hydra’s bond saves against an effect that would have them act against their allies (such as the confused condition, a dominate spell, or other mental effects that would give an ally the controlled condition), you can spend a Mythic Point to allow that character to attempt the save at mythic proficiency. If a member of the hydra’s bond fails a save against such an effect, other members automatically know that the target is controlled or under the influence of a mental effect. In addition, all members of the hydra’s bond gain a +2 circumstance bonus to any roll made to counteract that effect.

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 87 **Archetype** [Warshard Warrior](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=341) **Prerequisites** [Warshard Warrior Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8178) --- Your supernatural bond with your weapon infuses it with a powerful echo of your sentience, your memory, and even fragments of your very soul. When you would be killed while wielding your warshard weapon, you instead disappear and your warshard weapon falls to the ground. You reappear adjacent to your warshard weapon as soon as any sapient creature picks it up. If the creature is a close ally (such as another PC), you return to life with only 1 Hit Point. However, if a stranger does so, you return to life with full Hit Points. At your discretion, you can delay your return to life for up to 24 hours after a creature picks up the weapon, but you still return to life adjacent to your weapon (or as close to it as possible). If no one picks up your weapon within a week of your death, your soul enters the River of Souls, and you can be brought back to life using other means. No matter how you're brought back to life, you can [Call Warshard Weapon](/Actions.aspx?ID=3534) as a free action as soon as you regain consciousness. Alternatively, if no one picks up your warshard weapon within a week of your death, you can choose to fuse with your weapon rather than entering the River of Souls. You can no longer be brought back to life, but your soul remains bound to the weapon, and together you are an [intelligent item](/Rules.aspx?ID=3235), gaining the same Perception modifier, senses, communication, languages, attribute modifiers, and Will save as you. You retain the same Intelligence-, Wisdom-, and Charisma-based skills. You must still be carried and wielded, and your options are now limited to actions you can take as an intelligent item. You no longer gain or can spend Mythic Points, but as a weapon, you are still mythic. You can spend your actions to attack using the attack modifier with your warshard weapon you had in life, but your damage bonus uses the Strength modifier of your wielder instead of the Strength modifier you had in life. You gain the Impart Martial Wisdom action below, and you might gain other powers at the GM’s discretion, such as the ability to influence or even control your wielder. If you’re destroyed in this weapon form, your soul moves on to the River of Souls and you can be brought back to life using other means, but you must designate a new warshard weapon normally thereafter.
**Activate—Impart Martial Wisdom** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [mythic](/Traits.aspx?ID=835), [prediction](/Traits.aspx?ID=674)) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Effect** You call upon your experience in battle to see how best to attack a foe and give that knowledge to your wielder. Your wielder makes a Strike against a creature within reach or within your first range increment at mythic proficiency. This Strike ignores circumstance penalties to the attack roll and any flat check required due to the target being concealed or hidden.

[Uzunjati Recollection](/Feats.aspx?ID=1114); legendary in a [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) Skill

---

Your stories aren’t mere tales passed down from elder to youth or teacher to student. They’re the lived experiences of those you’ve met, and they’re the stuff of legend. When you use Uzunjati Recollection, if you’re legendary in the skill you use to Recall Knowledge, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the Recall Knowledge check, and the circumstance bonus to [Uzunjati Storytelling](/Feats.aspx?ID=1109) increases to +2.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs=""
>
[I've Been Here Before](/Feats.aspx?ID=8153) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Exploration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=66" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 77

**Archetype** [Heroic Scion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=339)

**Prerequisites**
[Heroic Scion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8151)

</column>

---

You adapt quickly to new settings and terrains. When you make your daily preparations in a region you’ve never visited before (such as a city, geographical region, or small demiplane, but not in a dungeon, structure, or other location that focuses on encounter mode play), you spend part of that time introspectively digging into the memories of your past life to get a feel for the adventure that awaits. Choose one of the following Exploration activities: [Avoid Notice](/Actions.aspx?ID=2622), [Defend](/Actions.aspx?ID=2623), [Investigate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2627), [Scout](/Actions.aspx?ID=2629), or [Search](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630). You perform that exploration activity at full speed rather than at half speed, and any skill check you attempt as a result of this Exploration activity is made at mythic proficiency. These benefits end as soon as you enter a new region, as determined by the GM.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Ice Crafter](/Feats.aspx?ID=3415) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monsters of Myth](/Sources.aspx?ID=107) pg. 10

**Archetype** [Pactbound Initiate](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=167)

**Prerequisites**
[Pactbound Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3414)

</column>

---

The ancient ice-crafting techniques of the saumen kar awaken within you. You become trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4), or become an expert if you were already trained. You gain the [Magical Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=812) skill feat. You can craft permanent items out of ice instead of metal or wood; these items are a translucent crystal-blue in color, resemble icicles and glacier ice, and have the same statistics and properties as [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=272), including the price and the ability to deal additional damage to certain kinds of creatures.

 Any creature who wields or wears a piece of ice-crafted equipment takes 1 cold damage each round from contact with the primal cold of the crafted ice.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 33

**Prerequisites**
[Beastbrood](/Feats.aspx?ID=2449)

**Requirements**
You're holding something sacred or precious to a creature, such as a relic or personal depiction of their deity or a precious personal memento.

</column>

---

You brandish the precious object you're holding menacingly, at once mocking it and threatening its safety. Attempt to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) the creature whose precious item you threaten. These conditions are both in addition to the normal effects of Demoralize. The creature is then temporarily immune to any Idol Threat using that specific object for 1 day.

---

Your wild, unique features betray your [agathion](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=216) birthright. Serene celestials from the plane of [Nirvana](/Planes.aspx?ID=20), agathions seek the peaceful path, ensuring a better world for all to coexist. Your halcyon demeanor leads you to search for peaceful resolution to conflict. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10). If you would automatically become trained in Nature (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You know the [Sylvan](/Languages.aspx?ID=10) language and gain the [Natural Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=815) skill feat.

<title level="2">Idyllkin leads to...</title>
[Agathion Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=2289), [Tranquil Sanctuary](/Feats.aspx?ID=2288)

    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Igneogenesis](/Feats.aspx?ID=4226) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 26

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Each 5-foot cube of stone created by the Igneogenesis impulse has the same statistics as stone (7 Hardness, 28 HP, BT 14)._

</column>

---

You can create a permanent stone object, either sculpting stone pulled directly from your kinetic gate or manipulating earth and stone around you. It must fit within one 5-foot cube that's adjacent to you and on solid ground, and you can make the object large enough to occupy the square. If you create the object underneath you or another willing creature, you cause the target to rise on top of the object; you can't create it under an unwilling creature. This impulse has an unlimited duration, but if you use Igneogenesis again, the object returns to its original location or form. You can spend 1 hour to use Igneogenesis as an [exploration](/Skills.aspx?ID=23) activity; in this case, the object is permanent and non-magical.

 The object can't include any intricate parts or moving pieces. You can attempt a [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) skill check as part of using this impulse to add details to your creation, such as a symbol, short message, or pattern (with the DC determined by the GM).

---
**Level (+3)** You can add an additional 5-foot cube to the object. Each cube must be contiguous.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Ignite the Sun](/Feats.aspx?ID=4250) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Light" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=100" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 29

</column>

---

The fires of creation become yours to control. You create a miniature sun in a 5-foot burst within 500 feet. A creature takes 7d6 fire damage any time it's in the miniature sun, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. A creature can take this damage no more than once per round. The sun sheds [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 500-foot emanation (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) for another 500 feet); this is sunlight for creatures with a particular vulnerability to sunlight.

 The sun lasts until the end of your next turn, but you can Sustain it up to 1 minute. The first time you Sustain the impulse each round, you can choose to increase the size of the sun's burst by 5 feet, then make it Fly up to 30 feet. The sun can move through creatures, damaging them as described above.

 The sun continually channels fire into you and your allies. You and each of your allies within the sun's light deal an additional 1d6 fire damage with all Strikes, spells that deal fire damage, and [impulses](/Traits.aspx?ID=502) that deal fire damage (except for Ignite the Sun itself). These aren't cumulative with multiple suns.

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 81 **Archetype** [Alter Ego](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=187) **Prerequisites** [Alter Ego Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3807) **Access** Members of the Firebrands at the rank of second mark or higher have access to this feat. --- There are times when skills or looks are not enough to convince someone of your identity, and you instead require adequate documentation. Replicating the methods of the Sapphire Butterfly, you've learned to use magic to forge a new identity as you need it. During your daily preparations, you can choose a blank piece of paper, journal, badge, or similar item normally used to display authority, to magically invest. You can use an Interact action to mentally outline the basic information that is displayed when that item is presented to another creature, such as a name, a title, connection to an existing group or agency, and other basic details. A more complex outline requires more time, at the GM's discretion. That creature must attempt a Will save against your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) DC. This item only works while you are holding it and appears blank if anyone else attempts to use it, though you can include others within the details of your outline. **Critical Success** The target sees the item as being entirely blank, and becomes immune to this effect until your next daily preparations.
**Success** The target sees only the basic information listed out in a simplistic manner, as described in the Interact action. Though not fully convinced, the target plays along, but this worsens the target's attitude toward you by one step.
**Failure** The target sees the information presented by the item in the proper format relevant to your situation, with the appropriate language, names, dates, signatures, and other details.
**Critical Failure** The target sees the information presented by the item as granting a higher level of authority than anticipated, and immediately treats you with the proper deference. As failure, and the target's attitude toward you immediately improves by one step.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs=""
>
[Imbue Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=7424) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 139

**Archetype** [Wildspell](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=295)

**Prerequisites**
[Wildspell Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7418)

**Trigger**
Your previous action was to [Cast a Spell](/Rules.aspx?ID=3144).

</column>

---

You pass the energy of your magic onto an ally, allowing another to release the spell. Upon completing the [Casting of a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734), instead of the normal effects of the spell, you imbue the energy of that spell to an ally that’s adjacent to you or within your spellsurge aura. You expend the spell, spell slot, or [Focus](/Rules.aspx?ID=285) Point as normal. At any time during the next hour, that ally can release the energy of the spell with a single action that has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) and [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) traits; they don’t need to expend any spell slots or Focus Points. All attributes of the spell are determined based on your original casting of the spell, including any [spellshape](/Traits.aspx?ID=513) feats used, but the ally is treated as the spellcaster for determining the origin of the spell and for making any choices the spell requires. If the spell must or can be [Sustained](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317), your ally takes the action to Sustain it. You can’t target yourself with this ability. If the spell isn’t released by the ally within 1 hour, the energy dissipates. You can only have one spell imbued at a time; additional uses of this ability cause previously imbued spells to [dissipate](/Rules.aspx?ID=2236) immediately.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Immobile Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=6999) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Yaoguai" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=833" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 86

**Prerequisites**
[Born of Item](/Heritages.aspx?ID=415) heritage, [Born of Elements](/Heritages.aspx?ID=414) heritage, or [Born of Vegetation](/Heritages.aspx?ID=416) heritage

</column>

---

You take on the shape you had before you awoke to hide in plain sight. When you Change Shape, you can assume the form of an immobile plant, object, or natural feature of Tiny, Small, or Medium size, as suits your heritage. Using your immobile form counts as setting up a disguise for the [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) use of [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38), except that you can Impersonate an object instead of a creature, it gives you a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through your disguise, and you add your level even if you’re untrained. You can speak while in immobile form, but you can’t attack, cast spells, or move.

---

Your commitment to ending all life earns you a measure of immortality, setting the stage for you to become a true Rider of the Apocalypse, possibly supplanting one of the Four. You gain the [daemon](/Traits.aspx?ID=568), [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600), and [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) traits, and so does your apocalypse mount, but your fates are ever more entwined. As long as your apocalypse mount lives, you don’t age and whenever your [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) or [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition would increase to 4 or more, it doesn’t increase. If you would be killed in any other way, you are instead reduced to 0 Hit Points, become [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95), and if your apocalypse mount is conscious, it instantly teleports to your side, picks you up, and attempts to flee the scene of danger. 

While you are conscious and within 30 feet of your apocalypse mount, it can’t be killed. If your apocalypse mount is reduced to 0 Hit Points, it immediately [stabilizes](/Rules.aspx?ID=1381) and its dying condition can’t increase. If its doomed condition would increase to 4 or more, it doesn’t increase. However, if you move more than 30 feet away from your apocalypse mount or go unconscious during this time, your apocalypse mount loses these benefits and might die.

Finally, when a living creature within 60 feet of you dies, it must attempt a Will saving throw against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. This is an [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631) effect. On a failure, that creature can’t be brought back to life for 24 hours. On a critical failure, you can chose to have that creature’s soul coalesce into a fist-sized soul gem (Hardness 2, HP 8) that appears in that creature’s space. That creature’s soul is trapped within the gem for 1 week, though you can make the gem permanent with a 10-minute ritual. Destroying the gem frees the soul within but doesn’t return the deceased creature to life. If a caster attempts to return to life a creature whose soul is trapped within a soul gem, they fail unless they succeed at a [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) check against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. A success causes the soul gem to shatter, allowing the creature to be returned to life as normal for the spell. Daemons and other fiends prize these soul gems, and they’re generally worth an amount relative to the level of a gem’s captive soul.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Impenetrable Fog](/Feats.aspx?ID=4275) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Overflow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=506" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 33

</column>

---

Fog condenses in a chaotic, swirling pattern, thick enough that it seems to push back against you. You call forth a fog bank in a 10-foot burst within 120 feet. All creatures in the fog are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4), and all creatures outside the fog become concealed to creatures within it. The fog is so magically dense it impedes movement, making the area [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453). The fog lasts until the end of your next turn, and you can Sustain the impulse up to 1 minute.

---
**Level (+3)** You can make the radius of the burst larger. Increase its maximum size by 5 feet.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Move" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=114" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=687" />

**Prerequisites**
Legendary in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1); [Quick Squeeze](/Feats.aspx?ID=5199)

**Requirements**

---

You find tiny imperfections and somehow fit yourself through them, possibly moving directly through the wall or floor. Your movement attempt fails if the wall or floor is made of something other than wood, plaster, or stone; is thicker than 10 feet; or contains even a thin layer of metal. If you have a climb Speed, you can use this ability to attempt to move through a ceiling.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Implausible Purchase](/Feats.aspx?ID=5971) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=818" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 113

**Archetype** [Twilight Talon](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=375) (Level 18)

**Prerequisites**
[Predictive Purchase](/Feats.aspx?ID=5953)

</column>

---

It seems impossible, but you've analyzed every angle and are able to just keep pulling out exactly the item you need, even in far-flung locations. You can use [Prescient Planner](/Feats.aspx?ID=5191) even if you have already used it after purchasing goods, and you can use it as a single action instead of a 2-action activity, during which you Interact to draw the item. In addition, five times per day, you can use Prescient Planner to pull out a common [consumable](/Traits.aspx?ID=564) item up to 6 levels lower than your level.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 47

**Requirements**
You're holding an [implement](/Implements.aspx).

</column>

---

Your implement supercharges your weapon to shoot an impossible volley or carve through your foes. Make a Strike with your weapon against each enemy within 30 feet of you. You don't increase your multiple attack penalty until after making all the attacks. If your weapon is a melee weapon and any of the attacks are outside your reach, you Release the weapon before the Strikes, and it returns to your grasp after all of them. If your hands are full when the weapon returns, it falls to the ground in your space.

By weakening your relation to the ground and strengthening your relation to the sky, you've learned to soar through the air, your [implement](/Implements.aspx) carrying you as surely as any broomstick or pestle. As long as you're holding a thaumaturge implement, you gain a fly Speed equal to your land Speed.

>
[Impose Order (Aphorite)](/Feats.aspx?ID=2487) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Aphorite" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=335" />
<trait label="Fortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=76" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 77

**Frequency**
once per day

**Trigger**
You would critically fail a skill check or suffer an effect with the [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=110) trait.

</column>

---

You shift the underlying fabric of reality to impose a baseline of order. If the trigger was a skill check, you instead receive a result of 10 + your proficiency bonus (don't apply any other bonuses, penalties, or modifiers). If the trigger was an effect with the misfortune trait, the misfortune and fortune effects cancel each other out as normal, negating the triggering misfortune effect.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 65

</column>

---

You can speak to inanimate objects, finding a magical spark within them similar to the one that animated you. You can cast [_stone tell_](/Spells.aspx?ID=310) once per day as an arcane innate spell, but instead of speaking with natural or worked stone, you speak with toys, statues, or other three-dimensional inanimate objects crafted to mimic a creature's appearance, regardless of their composition. The GM has discretion over which objects you can speak with and what they know, although objects generally have a good opinion of those who have cared for them and a poor opinion of those who have neglected or ignored them.

<title

    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Impossible Polymath](/Feats.aspx?ID=210) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Bard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=19" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 103

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), or Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13); [Esoteric Polymath](/Feats.aspx?ID=184)

</column>

---

Your esoteric formulas are so unusual that they allow you to dabble in magic from diverse traditions that other bards don’t understand. As long as you’re trained in Arcana, you can add arcane spells to your book from [Esoteric Polymath](/Feats.aspx?ID=184); as long as you’re trained in Nature, you can add primal spells to your book; and as long as you are trained in Religion, you can add divine spells to your book.

 Like your other spells in your book, you can add one of these spells from another tradition to your repertoire as an occult spell each day using Esoteric Polymath, but you can’t retain any spells from another tradition when you prepare again, even if you have Eclectic Polymath.

    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Impossible Riposte](/Feats.aspx?ID=1551) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Swashbuckler" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=321" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 93

**Prerequisites**
[Opportune Riposte](/Classes.aspx?ID=15)

</column>

---

Your ripostes can deflect attacks back at their source. You can use [Opportune Riposte](/Actions.aspx?ID=551) with a trigger of “A foe outside of your reach critically fails an attack roll against you” in addition to its usual trigger. When you use Opportune Riposte with this new trigger against a ranged attack, your Strike deflects some of the triggering effect back toward its source. Compare the result of your attack roll to the AC of the triggering foe. On a hit, you deal the normal amount of damage for your Strike, but the damage type changes to that of the triggering attack. For instance, if you used Opportune Riposte to deflect a [_ray of frost_](/Spells.aspx?ID=245), your Strike would deal cold damage instead of its normal damage type.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 192

**Archetype** [Cavalier](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=244)

**Prerequisites**
[Cavalier Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6286)

</column>

---

You've trained your mount to become a powerful force on the battlefield. The mount you gained through the [Cavalier Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6286) feat becomes a mature animal companion, granting it additional capabilities.

Your mount has greater independence. During an encounter, even if you don't use the [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400) action, your mount can still use 1 action that round on your turn to Strike or Stride (or [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310), [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312), or [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381) if it has that Speed). It can do this at any point during your turn, as long as you aren't currently taking an action. If it does, that's all the actions it gets that round—you can't Command it later.

<title level="2">Impressive Mount leads to...</title>
[Incredible Mount](/Feats.aspx?ID=6293)

---

Your performances inspire admiration and win you fans. You can Make an Impression using Performance instead of Diplomacy. If you spend at least 10 minutes performing in front of an audience, you can Make an Impression targeting up to 10 members of the audience who were there for the whole performance, without taking the normal penalty. The number of targets increases to 20 for a 1-hour performance and 50 for a 2-hour performance.

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 112 **Archetype** [Archfiend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=288) **Prerequisites** [Archfiend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7320) **Requirements** Your last action dealt damage to a creature. --- Rather than grant your foes the mercy of a swift death, you can consign them to suffer in an extradimensional prison with an appearance of your choosing. Spend 1 [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) to force a creature that you dealt damage to with your last action to attempt a Will saving throw against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. Regardless of the result, the target is temporarily immune to your Imprison Foe for 24 hours. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target is [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 2.
**Failure** The target is transported into a cell within your extradimensional dungeon for 1 minute. It is unable to leave or damage the cell in any way. [Teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) effects can’t carry the target outside the cell unless they can also traverse the planes, such as [_interplanar teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1576). At the end of each of its turns, it can attempt a new Will save to reduce the remaining duration it is imprisoned by 1 round or end it entirely on a critical success. When the duration ends, the target returns to the space it occupied when it was imprisoned, or to the nearest space if the original is now filled.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the target is [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) for the first round it is imprisoned.

[Improbable Elixirs](/Feats.aspx?ID=123) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=7" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 81

</column>

---

Your mastery of alchemical secrets enables you to replicate effects most believe can be achieved only via magic. Select a number of [potions](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&Subcategory=18) equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1); these potions must be of 9th level or lower. You gain formulas to create these potions as alchemical items with the [elixir](/Traits.aspx?ID=59) trait. When making these alchemical elixirs, you can substitute alchemical reagents for an equal value of magical components, and you can use [alchemist's tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2) (for [Quick Alchemy](/Feats.aspx?ID=667)) or an [alchemist's lab](/Equipment.aspx?ID=543) (for the [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) activity) instead of any other required tool kits. Other than that, the formula does not change. Once you've chosen the potion formulas, they can't be changed.

Select a number of potions equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1); these potions must be of 9th level or lower. Other than that, the formula doesn't change. Once you've chosen the potion formulas, they can't be changed.

</title>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 123

[Communal Healing](/Feats.aspx?ID=271)

---

You can direct excess channeled energy outward to benefit an ally. You can grant the Hit Points you would regain from Communal Healing to any one creature within the range of your [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=148) spell instead of yourself. You can also use Communal Healing when you target only yourself with a _heal_ spell, though if you do, you must grant the additional healing to someone other than yourself.

---

You can dash your foe to the ground with a single blow. When you use Knockdown, instead of making a Strike followed by a [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40), you can attempt a single Strike. If you do and your Strike hits, instead of rolling a check for your Trip attempt, you automatically apply the critical success effect of a Trip. If you used a two-handed melee weapon for the Strike, you can use the weapon's damage die size instead of the regular die size for the damage from a critical Trip.

---

You easily banish creatures with your weapon. You can use Swift Banishment as long as you have a spell slot of 5th level or higher remaining, even if you don’t have [_banishment_](/Spells.aspx?ID=19) prepared. You must sacrifice a prepared spell of 5th level or higher, and the _banishment_ effect you create is heightened to the level of that spell. Your weapon serves as the special material component of _banishment_, causing the target to take the –2 penalty to its save against any _banishment_ you cast using Swift Banishment.

May contain spoilers from Hell's Destiny **Source** [Pathfinder #223: Hell's Destiny](/Sources.aspx?ID=336) pg. 231 **Prerequisites** Master in [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) --- You’re a wild card on the battlefield, inventing unpredictable tactics and surprising foes. You employ one of these strategies, adding either your choice of the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) or [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) trait. Attempt a [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) check against the [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040) DC of a creature within 30 feet, after which the target becomes temporarily immune to further uses of Improvise Strategy for 1 hour. **Special** Once per day, if you lead a troop that has a [skirmish bond](/Rules.aspx?ID=3452), you can Improvise Strategy to attempt a Warfare Lore check against a standard DC for your troop’s level, rather than targeting a foe. If you succeed, your troop replaces its current skirmish bond with another of your choice until the end of your next turn. **Critical Success** The target gains one of the following conditions of your choice until the end of your next turn: [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) 1, [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65), [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58), or [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1. The target can end the effect by using either a single action with the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait to regain their bearings (if your strategy had the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) trait) or an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action to rub their eyes (if your strategy had the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) trait). In addition, the target isn’t temporarily immune to further uses of Improvise Strategy.
**Success** As critical success, but the target is temporarily immune to further uses of Improvise Strategy.
**Failure** The target is unaffected.
**Critical Failure** The target sees through the gambit, leaving you [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the beginning of your next turn.

You've learned to repair your equipment even in challenging circumstances, making use of what you have available. You can attempt to [Repair](/Actions.aspx?ID=42) an item without a [repair kit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=43), instead improvising tools out of your gear or found items. This adds 5 minutes to the time it takes to Repair the item. You can also Repair an item while on the move without needing a stable surface. This adds 10 minutes to the times it takes to Repair the item.

>
[Improvised Pummel](/Feats.aspx?ID=2100) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 199

**Archetype** [Weapon Improviser](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=82)

**Prerequisites**
[Weapon Improviser Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2099)

**Requirements**
You are wielding an improvised weapon.

</column>

---

You make a Strike with your wielded improvised weapon. You gain a +1 item bonus to the attack roll, and the Strike deals two weapon damage dice if it would have dealt fewer. If the attack is a critical hit, in addition to the effect of the critical hit, the improvised weapon breaks. If the item has a Hardness greater than your level, or if it's an [artifact](/Equipment.aspx?Category=45), [cursed item](/Equipment.aspx?Category=49), or other item that's difficult to break or destroy, the item doesn't break and the attack is a hit instead of a critical hit.

 At 12th level, your item bonus to the attack roll increases to +2 instead of +1, and at 16th level, the Strike deals three weapon damage dice if it would have dealt fewer, instead of two.

<title level="2">Improvised Pummel leads to...</title>
[Shattering Strike (Weapon Improviser)](/Feats.aspx?ID=2104)

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 221 **Archetype** [Weapon Improviser](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=269) **Prerequisites** [Weapon Improviser Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6440) --- When you make a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with an improvised weapon you're wielding, you gain a +1 item bonus to the attack roll, and you can have the Strike deal two weapon damage dice instead of the improvised weapon's normal number. If the attack is a critical hit, the improvised weapon breaks after the normal effects of a critical hit occur. If the item has a Hardness greater than your level, or if it's an [artifact](/Traits.aspx?ID=537), [cursed](/Traits.aspx?ID=567) item, or other item that's difficult to break or destroy, it doesn't break but the attack is a normal hit instead of a critical hit. You can choose not to get any of the effects of Improvised Pummel on a Strike if you don't want to risk breaking the item. At 12th level, the item bonus increases to +2, and at 16th level, the Strike deals three weapon damage dice instead of the improvised weapon's normal number.
If you're benefiting from [handwraps of mighty blows](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3086), you use the handwraps' item bonus if it's higher and can choose to use its number of damage dice. Any property runes from the handwraps also apply if you use the handwraps' number of weapon damage dice, provided they could apply to the improvised weapon (as determined by the GM). Improvised Pummel leads to... [Shattering Strike (Weapon Improviser)](/Feats.aspx?ID=6445)

fields.text: Feat 4 Improvised Pummel Archetype Source Player Core 2 pg. 221 Archetype Weapon Improviser Prerequisites Weapon Improviser Dedication When you make a Strike with an improvised weapon you're wielding, you gain a +1 item bonus to the attack roll, and you can have the Strike deal two weapon damage dice instead of the improvised weapon's normal number. If the attack is a critical hit, the improvised weapon breaks after the normal effects of a critical hit occur. If the item has a Hardness greater than your level, or if it's an artifact, cursed item, or other item that's difficult to break or destroy, it doesn't break but the attack is a normal hit instead of a critical hit. You can choose not to get any of the effects of Improvised Pummel on a Strike if you don't want to risk breaking the item. At 12th level, the item bonus increases to +2, and at 16th level, the Strike deals three weapon damage dice instead of the improvised weapon's normal number. If you're benefiting from handwraps of mighty blows, you use the handwraps' item bonus if it's higher and can choose to use its number of damage dice. Any property runes from the handwraps also apply if you use the handwraps' number of weapon damage dice, provided they could apply to the improvised weapon (as determined by the GM). You are skilled at making quick fixes to damaged equipment, but your fixes aren't meant to last forever. You make a quick repair to a [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=2) non-magical item in your possession. Until the item takes damage again, you can still use it as a [shoddy item](/Rules.aspx?ID=197) of its type. This repair restores no Hit Points, so the item is easy to destroy. Once the item is [Repaired](/Actions.aspx?ID=42) normally such that it is no longer broken, it is also no longer shoddy.

You can hastily patch damaged equipment together, but the temporary fix lacks the full care required for lasting repairs. You patch together a broken item possessed by you or an adjacent willing creature. Until the item takes damage again, it still functions as a [shoddy](/Rules.aspx?ID=2162) item of its type. If it's a magic item or another item with activations, it can't be activated while patched together, but can be used for normal functions (such as [Striking](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with a weapon or using [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) with a shield). This activity restores no Hit Points, so the item is easy to [destroy](/Rules.aspx?ID=2160) . Once the item is [Repaired](/Actions.aspx?ID=2384) normally such that it is no longer [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=60), it is also no longer shoddy.

**Prerequisites**

**Requirements**
You’re wearing or holding a [healer's toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2727).

</column>

---

“In lightning, there is life.” This lesson is whispered throughout Lepidstadt, and you can put it to practical use. You have integrated a miniature Stasian coil into your healer’s toolkit. You use the coil to gently shock a willing or unconscious ally within your reach, who gains 2d4 temporary Hit Points from the jolt. These temporary Hit Points last for 1 minute. These temporary Hit Points increase by 1d4 at 8th level and every 4 levels thereafter.

 A creature that has resistance or immunity to electricity is immune to this ability, and a creature that received temporary Hit Points from In Lightning, Life is temporarily immune to it for 24 hours.

When your skeletons and zombies attack, their skeletal claws and rotting hands clutch and tear flesh. Weaker foes are caught in their grip. You command your horde to perform a Mobbing Assault. Instead of being [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58), a creature who takes physical damage from failing the saving throw is [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) by your horde ([restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) on a critical failure). The DC to Escape from your horde is equal to your spell DC. Creatures grabbed by your horde that fail a saving throw against the horde's Mobbing Assault take 2d6 persistent bleed damage.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Incriminating Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=9389) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 108

</column>

---

You can attempt to blame someone else for your attempt to modify a target’s mind. If the next action you use is to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) with the [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) trait, choose a creature within 60 feet that the target can sense. The target will think that creature, instead of you, attempted to alter its mind when it succeeds at its save. If the target attempts to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302) on either you or the incriminated creature, they must compare the results to your spell DC instead of the target’s [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) DC. If the incriminated creature is obviously incapable of using magic, the target gains a +2 circumstance bonus to their [perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040) check to Sense Motive.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs=""
>
[Indomitable Shot](/Feats.aspx?ID=8185) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Attack" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=15" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 86

**Archetype** [Warshard Warrior](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=341)

**Prerequisites**
[Warshard Warrior Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8178)

**Requirements**
You are wielding a ranged warshard weapon.

</column>

---

You can fire a single shot that penetrates multiple foes. Spend 1 [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323), then fire a single shot from your ranged warshard weapon. You inflict your weapon’s damage on all creatures in a line, to a maximum distance equal to your weapon’s maximum range or until the line hits a solid object that’s either thicker than 5 feet or has a Hardness in excess of 20, whichever comes first. Each creature in the area attempts a basic Reflex save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, calculated at mythic proficiency. For each range increment beyond the first, a creature gains a cumulative +2 circumstance bonus to their Reflex save. This ability counts as two attacks when calculating your [multiple attack penalty](/Rules.aspx?ID=2289).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Induce Imbalance](/Feats.aspx?ID=7013) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=606" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 90

**Archetype** [Five-breath Vanguard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=272)

**Prerequisites**
[Five-breath Vanguard Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7011)

**Requirements**
You're in an elemental stance.

</column>

---

Your blows can disrupt the delicate balance of elemental energies that keep a body in good health. [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) the target using the unarmed attack associated with your current elemental stance. On a success, the target must attempt a Fortitude save against your class DC. On a failure, the target is [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) 2 until the end of your next turn. On a critical failure, the target is clumsy 3 for 1 minute. Elementals take a –2 circumstance penalty to their save.

<title level="2">Induce Imbalance leads to...</title>
[Five Breaths, One Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=7015)
