<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />
<trait label="Wizard" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=166" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 109

</column>

---

You imbue your spells with magical force to knock creatures back. If the next action you use is to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) that has an area of a [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385), [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386), [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387), or [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388); has no duration; and requires creatures to attempt a Reflex or Fortitude save, the spell unleashes a forceful blast that pushes creatures away, in addition to its other effects. Each creature that failed its save against the spell is pushed 5 feet, and those who critically failed are pushed 10 feet. If the spell is a cone, emanation, or a line, you push the creature away from yourself. If the spell is a burst, you push the creature away from the center of the burst.

[Know I Approach](/Feats.aspx?ID=9440) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Bugbear" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=744" />
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=590" />
<trait label="Fear" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=598" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=662" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 31

</column>

---

You can enact a short ritual to haunt prey you’ve singled out. Once per day during your daily preparations, you can take 10 minutes to target a creature whose name you know (and who is within 100 miles). Upon completion of the ritual, the target immediately knows you are seeking them out and must attempt a Will save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. If you have never met the target, it gains a +4 circumstance bonus to the save.

<column gap="tiny">

**Critical Success** The target knows of your intent, but is otherwise unaffected. The target becomes temporarily immune to this ritual for 1 week.

**Success** The target is wracked by a sense of dread at your approach. The next time the target sees you before your next daily preparations, they become [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1.

**Failure** As success, but the target becomes frightened 2 when they see you. They also become [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73) by the impending terror for 10 minutes after you perform this ritual.

**Critical Failure** As failure, but the target is [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 1 for as long as it is fatigued.

</column>

When you critically succeed at a [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) check about a creature, you can invoke your knowledge to make the creature take a –1 circumstance penalty to either AC and saves against the next attack you make against it, or the next spell you cast that it needs to defend against. You open a dozen small portals to some lightless, watery abyss in a 30-foot burst within 120 feet. The powerful tentacles of a kraken reach through to grab at each creature in the area. Each affected creature takes 8d6 damage depending on its Fortitude save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. You can Sustain the call up to 1 minute. The first time you Sustain it on each subsequent turn, each creature in the area not already [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) by the tentacles must attempt the save. **Success** The creature is unaffected.

The tentacles' [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) DC and AC are both equal to the higher of your class DC or spell DC. A creature can attack a tentacle to attempt to free the creature trapped by it; a tentacle is destroyed if it takes 30 or more damage in a single round.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Kreighton's Cognitive Crossover](/Feats.aspx?ID=2272) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 119

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All characters have access to this feat._

**Access**
Member of the Pathfinder Society.

**Trigger**
You gain no information from a [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) check (usually because you failed the [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) check) using one of the two skills you chose for this feat. 

</column>

---

Kreighton teaches his students that an agile mind can glean clues leading to the truth, even from the most unlikely of sources. You immediately reattempt the triggering check using the other chosen skill.

**Special** When you gain this feat, choose two of the following skills: [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4), [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) (any one), [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13), or [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14).

<title level="2">Scrolls Training</title>

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 119

The Society's Master of Scrolls, Kreighton Shaine (_Lost Omens Pathfinder Society Guide_ page 42), may be considered strange and absent-minded by his peers, but the elf venture-captain takes his duties quite seriously. Skilled in researching obscure subjects and unraveling inscrutable secrets, Kreighton teaches his students the value of an inquisitive mind.

**Related Feats**:

    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Lab Rat](/Feats.aspx?ID=1303) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Ratfolk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=234" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 23

</column>

---

You've spent more than your share of time in an alchemy lab. You might have been an alchemist yourself, an assistant, or perhaps even a test subject. Either way, you have been exposed to a wide variety of [alchemical poisons](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=9) and [elixirs](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=8), leaving you with increased tolerance of their effects. You have a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against poison and harmful effects from elixirs. If you roll a success on your saving throw against an elixir or poison, you get a critical success instead.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 17"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Landscape Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=6947) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Tanuki" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=830" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 69

**Frequency**
once per day

</column>

---

While walking down the road on a moonlit night, one might be puzzled to find a shop or hill that wasn’t there before. In reality, this is a tanuki at the height of their power. When you Change Shape, you can transform into a building or terrain feature up to 50 feet tall and up to 50 feet on a side. Mundane features of your landscape form function as normal—for instance, if you transform into a hot spring, the hot spring contains relaxing hot water, and if you transform into an inn, the inn contains bedrooms, beds, and delicious food—though no aspect of your landscape form can be an active hazard that can cause damage or impose conditions, and any objects created within your landscape form turn into leaves if taken outside of it. You can speak while in landscape form, but you can’t attack, cast spells, or move. You can remain in landscape form for up to 8 hours, and when you exit landscape form, it dissolves around anyone who was inside of it.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Larcenous Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=3384) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 124

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Agile Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=3369); [Pickpocket](/Feats.aspx?ID=818)

</column>

---

When you cast [_mage hand_](/Spells.aspx?ID=177), you can remove its duration, modify its range to 20 feet, and modify its target to be an attended object within the spell's Bulk limit that wouldn't be time-consuming to remove. Add the following to the spell's standard effects: If the creature attending the object is willing to have you take the item, _mage hand_ carries the item to you. If the creature is unwilling, you must attempt to [Steal](/Actions.aspx?ID=68) the target object with a [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) check. The usual restrictions on attempts to Steal an object apply, including the restrictions that you can't steal objects that would be extremely noticeable or time-consuming to remove (like worn shoes or armor or actively wielded objects) and you can't Steal from a creature in combat or otherwise on guard. On a successful Steal check, the _mage hand_ carries the item to you, and on a critical failure, you can't use this modification again for 1 hour. If you're a master in Thievery, you can attempt to Steal from a creature in combat or otherwise on guard, though if you do so, the spell's casting time increases by 1 action.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Larcenous Tail](/Feats.aspx?ID=2541) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Ganzi" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=339" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 97

**Prerequisites**
[Skillful Tail (Ganzi)](/Feats.aspx?ID=2538)

</column>

---

Your tail's chaotic and independent nature causes it to perform mischief even when you don't intend it, and it can somehow steal things it shouldn't be able to handle. You can use your tail to [Steal](/Actions.aspx?ID=68) an object, though your tail still can't hold onto it at the end of your action. If you have a hand free, you can transfer the stolen object to your hand. Otherwise, your tail surreptitiously drops it on the ground in your space, where you can grab it later. Observers other than your target who haven't witnessed you stealing something with your tail are usually distracted, meaning the GM will usually decrease their Perception DCs, as normal for Stealing something.

[Larger than Life (Guardian)](/Feats.aspx?ID=7832) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Guardian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=859" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 41

</column>

---

When you're clad in the heaviest of armors, you have an outsized presence. Though you don't get any larger, you're treated as one size larger for the purposes of affecting other creatures with actions like [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=2383), [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376), [Reposition](/Actions.aspx?ID=2379), [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380), and [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382) while wearing heavy armor. Similarly, you're treated as one size larger for the purposes of creatures affecting you with those same actions, as well as with [Swallow Whole](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=77) and similar actions, while wearing heavy armor.

**Access**

</column>

---

You’ve sworn yourself as a sentry for the Knights of Lastwall, the first line of defense against incursions by the Whispering Tyrant throughout Golarion. You become trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) and in Undead [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8); if you were already trained, you become an expert instead. Finally, you gain the [Reactive Shield](/Feats.aspx?ID=360) fighter feat.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the Lastwall sentry archetype.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [World Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=6) pg. 47

**Prerequisites**
[Lastwall Sentry Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=882)

</column>

---

You use your shield to protect your allies, not just yourself, especially against the undead. When you have a shield raised, you can use your [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839) reaction when an attack is made against an ally adjacent to you, in addition to its usual trigger. If you do, the shield prevents that ally from taking damage instead of you, following the normal rules for a [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839).

If an undead makes an attack against an ally within 10 feet, you can Step to become adjacent to your ally and then use [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839) as part of the same reaction.

You trace your lineage to [archons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=9): embodiments of heavenly virtues, guardians of the seven-tiered mountain of [Heaven](/Planes.aspx?ID=17), and nurturers of law and virtue within mortals. Your own virtue and orderly mind protect you from foes who would turn your emotions against you. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60) effects, and if you roll a success on a save against an emotion effect, you get a critical success instead.

---

When climbing, you can prepare routes for others to follow, and you can pull your allies up to avoid disaster. When your allies attempt to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=33) a route you set using the [Follow the Expert](/Actions.aspx?ID=514) exploration activity, if any of them critically fail their checks to Climb, you can attempt an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check against the same DC. If you succeed, your ally fails instead of critically failing. If you also critically fail, you both experience the consequences of the critical failure.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 161

**Archetypes** [Beastmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=50), [Undead Master](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=176) (Level 16)

**Prerequisites**
[Mature Beastmaster Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=1903); you have multiple animal companions

</column>

---

You can have up to two animal companions active at once. However, when you do, it's slightly more difficult to [Command](/Actions.aspx?ID=58) them. If you don't Command either of your companions, one of the two (your choice) can still use 1 action on your turn to Stride or Strike, as per [Mature Beastmaster Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=1903), but not both. When you Command an Animal, either choose one of the companions to take 2 actions, as normal, or else both companions can take 1 action to Stride or Strike. Either way, you can't Command an Animal to make either companion act again until your next turn.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Captain](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=332)

**Prerequisites**
[Captain Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7994)

</column>

---

You accept anyone who would follow you on your adventures. You can take followers from any common ancestry, and from uncommon or rare ancestries at the GM's discretion. Your follower gains the traits, size, Speeds, languages, and other special abilities listed in their ancestry. For example, elf followers have the elf and humanoid traits, a 30-foot  speed, low-light vision, and the typical languages for elves. Followers don't use their ancestry's Hit Points or attribute boosts and flaws. They also don't gain abilities that would allow them to use actions beyond the standard ones available to a follower, such as [Activating an Item](/Actions.aspx?ID=100) or [Casting a Spell.](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734)

<title level="3">Follower Ancestries</title> Since humans are the most populous ancestry in Golarion and don’t have any special abilities, they are presented as the default ancestry for followers. The GM can consider giving captains the Leader of All feat for free if humans aren’t the most common ancestry in their campaign setting, or if they aren’t concerned with players choosing to avoid human followers in favor of more mechanically powerful options.

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 90 **Prerequisites** Trained in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) **Requirements** You are adjacent to an enemy. --- You sweep your foe into your dance. Attempt a [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) check against an adjacent enemy's Will DC. If your swashbuckler's style is [battledancer](/Styles.aspx?ID=1) and you succeed, you gain panache. **Critical Success** Your foe is swept up in your dance. You both move up to 10 feet in the same direction, remaining adjacent to one another. Your movement doesn't trigger reactions from the target (and the target's movement doesn't trigger reactions because it's [forced movement](/Rules.aspx?ID=451)).
**Success** As critical success, but you both move only 5 feet.
**Failure** The foe doesn't follow your steps. You can move 5 feet if you choose, but this movement triggers reactions normally.
**Critical Failure** You stumble, falling [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) in your space.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=629" />
<trait label="Tanuki" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=830" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 67

</column>

---

You know how to run an enterprise that others would never be able to get off the ground—some say it’s your savvy acumen or jovial manner, but you know it’s because you can cut costs by transforming leaves into money. You can use [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) to [Earn Income](/Rules.aspx?ID=2635), and you gain a +1 status bonus to your check if you do so. The illusion doesn’t hold long, though! The GM rolls a secret d20; that many hours after concluding your check, the money transforms back, likely inviting consequences depending on how far the bills traveled from you in the time they were transformed.

>
[Leaping Hedgehog Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=7381) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 128

**Archetype** [Eternal Legend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=292)

**Prerequisites**
[Eternal Legend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7374)

</column>

---

You pounce toward an enemy and then barrel them over with one fluid movement, ending this maneuver with an attack that may catch them off-balance. [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298) horizontally toward an enemy you can see; treat your Speed as 30 feet or more for this Leap if it is less than 30 feet. If you end this movement adjacent to that enemy, attempt an [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) check to [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=2370) that enemy’s space. On a success, the target is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88). You then Strike that same enemy. If the target has been knocked prone, you can spend 1 [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) as part of this Strike to make it at mythic proficiency.

If you’re slain, any of your knights who touches your corpse can choose to take up your mantle; over the course of 10 minutes, they don your equipment, replace their attribute modifiers with yours, replace their skills and feats with yours, and become you for all intents and purposes, retaining only their [ancestry](/Rules.aspx?ID=3286), [heritage](/Rules.aspx?ID=2083), and ancestry feats. If you’re later returned to life, you can choose to reclaim your mantle from your former knight; if you do so, they revert to their previous state, and you reclaim all that was yours. Otherwise, you can choose to live a new life, retraining all your skills and feats while adopting a new name and identity.

Your skill with languages and codes is so great that you can decipher information with little more than a quick read through a text. You can Decipher Writing using Society while reading at normal speed. If you slow down and spend the full amount of time that’s ordinarily required and roll a success, you get a critical success; if you critically succeed while spending the normal amount of time, you gain a nearly word-for-word understanding of the document.

You know the wilderness so well that you can help your party travel through it with ease. When you are setting the path for your party through wilderness terrain, your party gains a +10-foot circumstance bonus to its Speed for the purpose of calculating the party's travel speed, your party's travel speed doesn't decrease in difficult terrain, and greater difficult terrain halves your party's travel speed instead of reducing it to a third. This doesn't increase your party's Speed during an encounter or allow your party to ignore difficult terrain during an encounter.

**Prerequisites**
[Captain Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7994); legendary in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40)

</column>

---

Your fame has spread throughout the lands. When you first attempt to [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394) or [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) on an intelligent creature, the GM rolls a secret DC 11 flat check to see if they have heard of you. On a success, you gain a +2 circumstance modifier to the skill check for that action. The GM can adjust this flat check as appropriate for circumstances in which you may be more or less known. 

You can also leverage your notoriety and your network of assistants and admirers to earn money. You can [Earn Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=2364) using the skill you used to meet the prerequisites of this feat. When you do, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the  check; this bonus increases to a +3 if you have the [Cadre](/Feats.aspx?ID=7998) feat, as your retainers praise your deeds and find those who might  pay to meet you.

You can Unleash Yaoguai Might any number of times per day. Once per day when you Unleash Yaoguai Might, you can gain one of the following additional benefits, which persists for 1 minute or until you Change Shape again.
  • Your body grows to impossible heights. Your [_enlarge_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1514) effect is heightened to 4th rank.
  • Your spiritual power erupts to punish your enemies. You deal an additional 1d4 spirit damage with all [Strikes](/Rules.aspx?ID=1606) and [attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=540) spells, and your Strikes and attack spells gain the [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) trait.
  • You can leap off the air itself. You gain the effects of the [_fly_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1534) spell.

---

You can negotiate incredibly quickly in adverse situations. You attempt to Make an Impression and then Request your opponent cease their current activity and engage in negotiations. You take a –5 penalty to your Diplomacy check. Generally, the DC of this check is the creature’s Will DC, although your GM may modify it based on the situation. Some creatures may be unable to stop regardless of their personal desires, and even those who agree to parley might ultimately find your arguments lacking and return to violence.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 257

**Prerequisites**
Legendary in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12); [Virtuosic Performer](/Feats.aspx?ID=5235)

</column>

---

Your fame has spread throughout the lands. Creatures who have any listed skill in Society have heard of you and usually have an attitude toward you one step better than normal, depending on your reputation and the creature’s disposition. For instance, if you’re well-known for cruel and demanding behavior, creatures might be intimidated by you, rather than be friendly toward you. When you Earn Income with Performance, you attract higher-level audiences than your location would allow, as audiences flock to see you. For instance, rulers and angels might travel to your small tower in the woods to hear you perform. Typically, this increases the audiences available to your level or by two levels, whichever is higher.

</column>

---

Your ability to Steal defies belief. You can attempt to Steal something that is actively wielded or that would be extremely noticeable or time consuming to remove (like worn shoes or armor). You must do so slowly and carefully, spending at least 1 minute (and significantly longer for items that are normally time consuming to remove, like armor). Throughout this duration you must have some means of staying hidden, such as the cover of darkness or a bustling crowd. Even if you succeed, if the item is extremely prominent—like a suit of full plate armor—onlookers will quickly notice it’s gone after you steal it.

>
[Lepidstadt Surgeon Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7472) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 94

**Archetype** [Lepidstadt Surgeon](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=302)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42); attended the University of Lepidstadt

</column>

---

Before everything else, before the blood and the monsters and the Stasian technology and the horror, you are a doctor. You are, in fact, an exceptionally good doctor. You become an expert in Medicine. When you successfully [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2396) to stabilize a [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) creature that doesn’t yet have the [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=99) condition, it regains 2d8 Hit Points; this healing increases by 10 when you are a master of Medicine and by another 10 when you are legendary in Medicine. When you successfully Administer First Aid to stop bleeding, the target rolls the flat check (with lowered DC for an assisted recovery) twice and takes the better result; this is a fortune effect.

<title level="2">Lepidstadt Surgeon Dedication leads to...</title>
[Artery Map](/Feats.aspx?ID=7475), [Beautiful Knifework](/Feats.aspx?ID=7477), [In Lightning, Life](/Feats.aspx?ID=7473), [Rise, My Creature!](/Feats.aspx?ID=7474), [Stand Back, I'm a Doctor!](/Feats.aspx?ID=7480)

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 127

**Prerequisites**
[leaf order](/DruidicOrders.aspx?ID=2)

</column>

---

You call a minor spirit of nature into a plant body, creating a leshy companion to aid you in your spellcasting. You gain a familiar, which has your choice of either the [plant](/Familiars.aspx?ID=120) or [fungus](/Familiars.aspx?ID=114) familiar ability; this doesn't count against your usual limit of familiar abilities (typically 2). The spirit you call has a more tenuous connection to its plant body than fully independent leshies, so it is Tiny in size like other familiars.

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 124 **Prerequisites** [leaf order](/DruidicOrders.aspx?ID=2) --- The leaf order's secrets allow your familiar to take advantage of its leshy form. You can select one additional familiar ability each day, which must be one of the following leshy familiar abilities. You can't select more than one leshy familiar ability at a time.
  • **Grasping Tendrils** Your familiar can extend vines or similar tendrils, increasing its reach to 15 feet.
  • **Purify Air** Your familiar recycles air, providing enough oxygen for a Medium creature in areas with stale air, such as a sealed chamber or [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) space. If the leshy is within the area of an [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=96) poison effect or an effect that relies on smell, creatures within a 15-foot emanation from the leshy gain a +2 circumstance bonus to their saving throws against the effect.
  • **Verdant Burst** When your familiar dies, it releases its primal energy to cast the 3-action version of [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=148), heightened to a level 1 lower than your highest-level spell slot. The heal spell gains a status bonus equal to twice the spell's level to the Hit Points it restores to [plants](/Traits.aspx?ID=125). You must be able to cast 2nd-level spells using spell slots to select this familiar ability.

>
[Let Death Be My Weapon](/Feats.aspx?ID=8159) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 78

**Archetype** [Heroic Scion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=339)

**Prerequisites**
[Heroic Scion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8151)

</column>

---

You recall your death in vivid detail, and the fear, pain, and uncertainty you suffered are blunted by the truth of your reincarnation. Pain and agony brought on by your foes can be endured and even turned back upon them when you feel yourself at death’s door. Whenever you have the [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67), [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69), or [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=99) condition, you gain that condition’s value as a status bonus to damage rolls when you make melee or ranged weapon Strikes. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #165: Eyes of Empty Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=81) pg. 77

**Archetype** [Drow Shootist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=90)

**Prerequisites**
[Drow Shootist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2683); Trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)

</column>

---

You've learned more than the use of hand crossbows from drow lore. During your daily preparations, you can prepare a dose of [lethargy poison](/Equipment.aspx?ID=120) from ordinary materials in a wilderness or urban area. If you're an expert in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4), you can instead craft a dose of [stupor poison](/Equipment.aspx?ID=939). You can prepare two doses (of either poison) if you're a master in Crafting and three doses if you're legendary in Crafting. The save DC for this poison is equal to your class DC. Only you can use these poisons, and they expire the next time you make your daily preparations. The GM might decide that the area you're in is too barren to provide the materials you need for this feat.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=615" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 232

**Prerequisites**
[Courtly Graces](/Feats.aspx?ID=5138) or [Streetwise](/Feats.aspx?ID=5218); Expert in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)

</column>

---

You know the right people who can get things done for you in certain circles. Once per week, when you're in an area that has an established group of influential nobles, mercantile elites, or the like (if you have Courtly Graces), or a network of unsavory characters such as a thieves' guild (if you have Streetwise), you can use Society to [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) a favor or aid from those people as if they were friendly to you. Your request must make sense for the type of people you contact. For instance, a member of the royal court could secure you a proper invitation to a fancy ball, while a local burglar could point out a way to stealthily infiltrate that same party. If you critically succeed this check, your connection gives a piece of helpful advice or lets you in on a small secret, granting you or a member of your party a +2 circumstance bonus to the first skill check you attempt when acting on the favor. If you critically fail this check, you might have to perform some service for your connection to get back in their good graces, as determined by the GM.

fields.text: Feat 2 Leverage Connections Uncommon General Skill Source Player Core 2 pg. 232 Prerequisites Courtly Graces or Streetwise; Expert in Society You know the right people who can get things done for you in certain circles. Once per week, when you're in an area that has an established group of influential nobles, mercantile elites, or the like (if you have Courtly Graces), or a network of unsavory characters such as a thieves' guild (if you have Streetwise), you can use Society to Request a favor or aid from those people as if they were friendly to you. Your request must make sense for the type of people you contact. For instance, a member of the royal court could secure you a proper invitation to a fancy ball, while a local burglar could point out a way to stealthily infiltrate that same party. If you critically succeed this check, your connection gives a piece of helpful advice or lets you in on a small secret, granting you or a member of your party a +2 circumstance bonus to the first skill check you attempt when acting on the favor. If you critically fail this check, you might have to perform some service for your connection to get back in their good graces, as determined by the GM.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Move" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=658" />

<column gap="tiny">

---

You can wrap your lash around a tree branch or railing, then pull yourself where you need to go. Choose a solid anchor point within reach of your lash. You [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) up to your Speed as you pivot around the anchor, ending in an open space where the anchor is still within reach of your lash. If you don't end your turn in a space you could stand, you fall.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 27

**Archetype** [Soul Warden](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=173)

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
[Soul Warden Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3466)

**Requirements**
Your spiral is glowing.

</column>

---

The light flows from your sigil of [Pharasma](/Deities.aspx?ID=14) to shatter the bonds imprisoning a soul. You attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) a [possession](/Traits.aspx?ID=129) effect, or an effect, object, or spell that is imprisoning a soul (such as [_bind soul_](/Spells.aspx?ID=21), a _soul gem_, or a [devourer's](/Monsters.aspx?ID=612) devoured souls). You must be within 60 feet of the possessed creature or object, or of the receptacle imprisoning the soul. Your counteract level is half your level rounded up, and your counteract modifier is your divine spell DC – 10. If the attempt fails, you can't use Liberate Soul against that particular effect again unless circumstances have changed drastically, as determined by the GM.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Liberating Dive](/Feats.aspx?ID=8979) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Hell's Destiny</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=527" />
<trait label="Composite" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=501" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Metal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=505" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=676" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #223: Hell's Destiny](/Sources.aspx?ID=336) pg. 229

</column>

---

You sprout wings with steel feathers, resembling those of the [celestial](/Traits.aspx?ID=551) [Talmandor](/NPCs.aspx?ID=4835). With a powerful flap, the wings propel you across the battlefield, slicing foes and restraints along your path. Until the end of your turn, you gain a [fly Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350) equal to your land Speed or 40 feet, whichever is greater. You then [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) up to your Speed, and this movement doesn't trigger reactions.

Choose one foe and one ally you're adjacent to at any point during this movement. Using one wing's sharpened edge, you can use a 1-action [Elemental Blast](/Actions.aspx?ID=2125) as a melee Strike using the metal element against the foe. With the other wing, you can help the ally break free of an effect [grabbing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), [restraining](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90), [immobilizing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81), or [paralyzing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85) them; they either attempt a new save against one such effect that allows a save, or they attempt to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) as a free action. The ally can use your [impulse](/Traits.aspx?ID=502) attack modifier in place of their unarmed attack modifier or skill check modifier.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 35

**Archetype** [Steel Falcon](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=374)

**Prerequisites**
[Steel Falcon Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8848); Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

</column>

---

Your devotion to Andoran's ideals is as much spiritual as philosophical. You gain the cleric's [Domain Initiate](/Feats.aspx?ID=4644) feat but must select [freedom](/Domains.aspx?ID=77), [truth](/Domains.aspx?ID=95), or [zeal](/Domains.aspx?ID=100) as your domain. You cast that domain's domain spell as a divine focus spell, and you [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=2621) by contemplating or spreading the ideas of the Common Rule rather than praying to a god. When an ability would manifest a divine symbol—such as the [_word of truth_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1842) focus spell—it instead manifests as an eagle clutching a sword in its talons.

**Special** You can take this feat multiple times, selecting a different domain each time.

>
[Lich Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3513) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 50

**Archetype** [Lich](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=179)

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4); living creature, ability to cast 6th-level or higher spells from spell slots, completed ritual to become a lich and crafted a _soul cage_

</column>

---

After years of study and careful planning, you finally completed a _soul cage_ to house your soul and successfully performed a ritual to transform yourself into a lich. Now, neither death nor time can prevent you from pursuing your studies and achieving your grand ambitions. You gain the undead trait and the [basic undead benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=1694). Your undead craving is for knowledge.

 You gain a unique [_soul cage_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1545)—a magic item that houses your soul. Whenever you would die, your soul flees to the _soul cage_ to allow you to be rebuilt. As long as your soul cage exists, you can't truly be destroyed.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the lich archetype.

<title level="2">Lich Dedication leads to...</title>
[Bolster Soul Cage](/Feats.aspx?ID=3517), [Drain Soul Cage](/Feats.aspx?ID=3514), [Enshroud Soul Cage](/Feats.aspx?ID=3515), [Hand of the Lich](/Feats.aspx?ID=3516), [Spell Gem](/Feats.aspx?ID=3518)

</column>

---

You're adept at noticing the tells of a liar—sweat, flushing, a quavering voice, a quickening pulse. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=85) and to Perception DCs against attempts to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47) to you. When you determine someone is lying to you, you can use their deceit to your advantage to gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the next [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7), or [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) check you attempt against that creature within the next minute.

---

You can use Deception to weave traps to trip up anyone trying to deceive you. If you can engage in conversation with someone trying to Lie to you, use your Deception DC if it is higher than your Perception DC to determine whether they succeed. This doesn’t apply if you don’t have a back-and-forth dialogue, such as when someone attempts to Lie during a long speech.

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Life Leap](/Feats.aspx?ID=1420) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gnome" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=80" />
<trait label="Move" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=114" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=156" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 44

**Requirements**
You must be adjacent to a living creature.

</column>

---

You phase through a space that a living creature occupies in a flash, spontaneously appearing on the opposite side of it in a vibrant display of colorful light. You move from your current location to another location that's still adjacent to the same living creature, but on the opposite side or corner of the creature's space. To determine whether a position is valid, use the same rules as for flanking: a line through the center of the two spaces must pass through opposite sides or corners of the creature's space.

 You pass through the creature's life force, appearing in the selected location; this doesn't trigger reactions based on movement. You must be able to see your destination, and you can't move farther than your Speed would allow.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=623" />
<trait label="Samsaran" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=828" />
<trait label="Vitality" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=509" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 56

</column>

---

Your journey to enlightenment has made your blood possess nigh-immortal properties, allowing you to heal others. You sacrifice some of your vitality to heal another willing living creature that’s adjacent to you, coating its wounds with your blood. You lose 3d6 Hit Points, plus an additional 1d6 Hit Points for every 2 levels you have beyond 10th. This damage can’t be resisted, prevented, or negated in any way. The target creature regains a number of Hit Points equal to the damage you took. Creatures you heal in this manner are then temporarily immune to your Life’s Blood for 24 hours.

For an instant, you transform yourself into a being of pure lightning and fly forward, shocking anyone in your way. You propel yourself forward in a 30-foot line. You can move through creatures during this movement, and this movement doesn't trigger reactions that are triggered by movement. Each creature you move through takes 2d12 electricity damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. You return to your normal form in the final square of the line. If you're in the air, you fall unless you have a fly Speed.

---
**Level (+3)** The length of the line increases by 5 feet, and the damage increases by 1d12.

    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Lingering Bomb](/Feats.aspx?ID=9534) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Additive" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=795" />
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=812" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 199

**Prerequisites**
[bomber research field](/ResearchFields.aspx?ID=5)

</column>

---

You can mix slow-burning fuels into your alchemical bombs that deal [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), making their effects linger. When you Strike with the bomb, it deals no damage on a direct hit (though it still deals [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage and applies other effects such as saving throws); you can also Strike an empty space with the bomb, automatically succeeding on your attack roll. On a failure, success, or critical success, the bomb’s contents spread in the target’s space, creating a lingering alchemical flame. The first time a creature enters the flame on its turn or starts its turn in the flame, it takes damage of the same amount and type as the bomb’s persistent damage. The flame lasts for 1 minute or until an adjacent creature uses an Interact action to smother it.

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Aftermath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=424" />
<trait label="Cold" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=27" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 55

**Prerequisites**
You've been brought to 0 Hit Points by an enemy that has the [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) trait or an enemy's ability that has the cold trait.

</column>

---

The chill of ice entered your veins and never left, adjusting the internal temperature of your body. Your breath comes out in puffs, and your skin is as cold and smooth as the ice in your veins. You can cast [_ray of frost_](/Spells.aspx?ID=245) as a primal innate cantrip. You gain resistance to cold damage equal to half your level, and you're protected from [severe cold temperatures](/Rules.aspx?ID=642).

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Reincarnated" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=783" />
<trait label="Universal Ancestry" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=467" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #199: To Bloom Below the Web](/Sources.aspx?ID=225) pg. 80

</column>

---

You achieved fluency in different languages with each reincarnation, and your brain remembers much of the grammar, idioms, and obscenities that you spouted in old lives. You gain [_tongues_](/Spells.aspx?ID=340) as a 5th-level occult innate spell that you can cast once a day on yourself only. While the spell is active, you get a +2 circumstance bonus to Diplomacy checks while speaking to a creature in a language other than Common.

member of the Lion Blades; Trained in [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45)

**Access**
You’re from Taldor.

</column>

---

Your Lion Blade spy training helps you conceal yourself and your identity. You become trained in your choice of [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) or [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48); if you were already trained in that skill, you become an expert instead. You also gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) skill feat for [Espionage Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41). If you were already trained in Espionage Lore, you also become trained in a Lore skill of your choice.

You never take circumstance penalties for attempting to take a disguise of a different ancestry, age, and so on, as long as the disguised form is appropriate for your size.

<title level="2">Lion Blade Dedication leads to...</title>
[Expeditious Advance](/Feats.aspx?ID=7728), [Flickering Twirl](/Feats.aspx?ID=7732), [Inspiring Recitation](/Feats.aspx?ID=7725), [Lion's Magic](/Feats.aspx?ID=7730), [Lost in the Crowd](/Feats.aspx?ID=7726), [Slowing Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=7733), [Spy's Countermeasures](/Feats.aspx?ID=7731), [Stunning Surprise](/Feats.aspx?ID=7734)

Your kingdom's economy can liquidate resources in an emergency when funding runs out. The first time during a Kingdom turn in which you are forced to spend RP as the result of a failed skill check or a dangerous event, and that expense reduces you to 0 RP, you may instead reduce your RP to 1 and treat the expense as if it were paid in full. >
[Live Ammunition](/Feats.aspx?ID=3227) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 129

**Archetype** [Artillerist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=115)

**Prerequisites**
[Artillerist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3222)

</column>

---

There are generally few things as ill-advised as being shot out of a cannon or launched by a trebuchet, but people use the tactic every so often in a desperate situation. While it's more humane to use this strategy with mindless [constructs](/Traits.aspx?ID=35) or [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), occasionally an exceedingly foolhardy adventurer demands the opportunity to try it. Loading a creature requires two additional [Load](/Rules.aspx?ID=1624) actions, which you must conduct personally. The creature must be willing, [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38), or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33) throughout the process, and the [siege weapon](/SiegeWeapons.aspx) must be physically capable of firing the creature in question, based on their size and shape. Typically, that means ballistas don't qualify, for example—nor do auto-catapults which require specifically-sized balls—but normal catapults and onagers work just fine. When you [Launch](/Rules.aspx?ID=1626) the weapon, if the weapon usually targets an area, you target a single 5-foot square instead. The siege weapon deals its normal damage to its target, or to the modified area, and to the creature fired.

<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />

---

You tap into the future to steal a bit of time from yourself a few seconds from now that you can use immediately. You become [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) for 1 round, and can use the extra action to take any basic or [specialty basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2344) 1-action action. You gain this extra action immediately and can use it this turn. At the end of your turn, you become [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 and are immune to the quickened condition until the end of your next turn.

    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Living Bonfire](/Feats.aspx?ID=4298) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Composite" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=501" />
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 36

</column>

---

Roots and branches of living wood writhe in elemental fire at your command, forming a bonfire fearsome enough to scare off predators in the night. You conjure a bonfire in an unoccupied 10-foot-square space within 30 feet. The bonfire burns for 10 hours, providing all the benefits of a normal campfire. If you use this impulse again, any previous one ends.

 When you make a wood ranged [_Elemental Blast_](/Actions.aspx?ID=2125), you can have it come from the bonfire instead of you, flinging burning logs. This blast deals an additional 1d6 fire damage. Each time you do this, the size of the bonfire is reduced by one 5-foot square. If all the squares are removed, the impulse ends.

---
**Level (+5)** The fire damage increases by 1d6.

    right="Feat 20"
    pfs=""
>
[Living Epic](/Feats.aspx?ID=7391) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 129

**Archetype** [Eternal Legend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=292)

**Prerequisites**
[Eternal Legend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7374)

</column>

---

You are a living legend, a being who cannot be claimed by [death](/Rules.aspx?ID=2329), as death has already passed you. You are beyond whatever they wish to make you. When you would be killed, you instead disappear. You reappear anywhere where your name is spoken in the next week. Your name must be said in the context of recounting one of your exploits, including your death. If the person speaking your name is a close ally (such as another PC), you return to life with only 1 Hit Point. However, if a stranger speaks your name, you return to life with full Hit Points and you gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, Perception, saving throws, and skill checks for 1 week. If no one speaks your name within a week of your death, your soul enters the River of Souls, and you can be brought back to life using other means.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Living for the Applause](/Feats.aspx?ID=4142) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 80

**Archetype** [Gladiator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=251)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Gladiator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1976)

**Access**
Members of the Firebrands at the rank of second mark or higher have access to this feat.

**Trigger**
You would be reduced to 0 Hit Points (but not immediately killed) during a combat encounter that has spectators.

</column>

---

Nothing can stop you as long as you have an audience cheering you on. The attention reinvigorates you and keeps you from being knocked out. You remain at 1 Hit Point, and your [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=42) condition increases by 1.

 In addition, attempt a [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) check; the DC is determined by the GM but is typically the [standard DC for your level](/Rules.aspx?ID=554) or the DC to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) on the spectators, whichever is higher. On a success, the crowd erupts in applause and cheers at your comeback, much to the dismay of your enemies. Concern for the crowd's reaction should your opponent deliver a finishing blow gives you a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the end of your next turn. On a critical success, you don't expend your daily use of Living for the Applause and can use the reaction an additional time on the same day.

---

You have reached heights of power equaling [Razmir’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=357) himself. You can [Craft](/Rules.aspx?ID=2634) your [Razmiri mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3593)  out of porcelain laced with precious metals, or upgrade your existing mask to a porcelain one in the same time it takes to Craft one made of iron. A porcelain Razmiri mask grants a +4 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389) or [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390), is an 18th-level item, and is an apex item that increases your Charisma modifier by 1 or increases it to +4, whichever would give you a higher score. It also gives you the following activation in addition to those granted by the standard, silver, and gold masks.

**Activate—Power of the Living God** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You demand power from the world, using your mask as a locus to force reality to bend to your will. You cast [_manifestation_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1592) as a 10th-rank [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) spell, but no matter what spell you emulate with it, that spell has the [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631) trait.

    right="Feat 2"

>
[Living Nexus Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9338) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 96

**Archetype** [Living Nexus](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=392)

**Prerequisites**
trained in martial weapons; Trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

</column>

---

Whether through happenstance or hours of rigorous training, you have discovered within yourself the ability to breathe in the magic around you.

You have an invisible, internal nexus of energy and have learned how to control your absorption of others’ magical energy and store it in this internal nexus. You gain the Absorb Magic reaction and the Overflowing Blade action. The DC for an ability gained via this archetype is either your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, and is called your nexus DC. 

**Absorb Magic** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Requirements** You are not overflowing; **Trigger** Another creature within 30 feet [Casts a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=3521) or uses an action, activity, or reaction with the [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), or [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) trait; **Effect** You breathe in a small fraction of the magic produced by the triggering effect, storing it in your internal nexus. You become overflowing. You remain overflowing for up to 1 minute before the stored magical energy fades. While overflowing, you gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against effects with the arcane, divine, magical, occult, and primal traits. This bonus becomes +2 at 15th level.

**Overflowing Blade** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Requirements** You are overflowing; **Effect** You conduct the magic in your internal nexus to coat your weapon or unarmed strike, empowering it with magical energy for a devastating attack. Make a melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167). If the Strike hits, you deal an additional 1d4 force damage. At 10th level, the additional damage increases to 2d4 force damage. At 18th level, the additional damage increases to 3d4 force damage. You are no longer overflowing.

You have an invisible, internal nexus of energy and have learned how to control your absorption of others’ magical energy and store it in this internal nexus. You gain the Absorb Magic reaction and the Overflowing Blade action. The DC for an ability gained via this archetype is either your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, and is called your nexus DC. Absorb Magic Reaction (concentrate, magical) Requirements You are not overflowing; Trigger Another creature within 30 feet Casts a Spell or uses an action, activity, or reaction with the arcane, divine, magical, occult, or primal trait; Effect You breathe in a small fraction of the magic produced by the triggering effect, storing it in your internal nexus. You become overflowing. You remain overflowing for up to 1 minute before the stored magical energy fades. While overflowing, you gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against effects with the arcane, divine, magical, occult, and primal traits. This bonus becomes +2 at 15th level. Overflowing Blade Single Action (concentrate, force, magical) Requirements You are overflowing; Effect You conduct the magic in your internal nexus to coat your weapon or unarmed strike, empowering it with magical energy for a devastating attack. Make a melee Strike. If the Strike hits, you deal an additional 1d4 force damage. At 10th level, the additional damage increases to 2d4 force damage. You’ve bridged a connection between the runes on your body and the magic of runestones, allowing you to place an armor rune on your living flesh. Your body becomes living stone. You don't need to eat or drink and need only 6 hours of rest to feel well rested. You must still rest at least 8 hours and spend 1 hour of preparation to regain resources usable only a limited number of times per day, such as spell slots. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against [diseases](/Traits.aspx?ID=46), [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), and effects that would cause the [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28) or [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) conditions. When you roll a successful saving throw against a disease or poison, you get a critical success instead.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Living Vessel Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3815) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 140

**Archetype** [Living Vessel](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=188)

</column>

---

Whether willingly or not, you've become a vessel for a being of unimaginable power. You and your GM should work together to determine the being's nature and decide how much you know and how much remains a mystery to you for now. Some decisions might influence your options later. You might need to decide whether the entity is a [demon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=28), for instance, to know if you qualify for later feats.

 You need to spend at least an hour each day assuaging the entity within you or you take a –1 penalty to Will saves for 24 hours. The process of assuaging the entity is determined together between you and the GM. It might be as simple as meditating with the entity to learn more about them, but it might be as extreme as committing gruesome, unspeakable sacrifices to keep their unknowable blessings. After a full week of failing to assuage your entity, you become [doomed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9), and you can't remove or ameliorate the condition until you allow your entity to take full possession of your body for 24 hours, during which time it pursues its own agenda.

 You also gain the Entity's Resurgence reaction, allowing you to unleash your entity in lieu of falling [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38), though at the risk of letting it enact its will.

 **Entity's Resurgence** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** You would be reduced to 0 Hit Points but not immediately killed; **Effect** Instead of letting you fall unconscious, your entity takes control. You remain at 1 Hit Point and gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level + your key ability modifier that last for 1 minute. However, the entity is in control for 1 minute or until you fall unconscious, whichever comes first.

 While the entity is in control, you gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls, and the GM usually controls your character, roleplaying the entity. The GM might decide to have you roleplay the entity instead, but they retain final say over any decisions you make. No matter the entity's nature, the entity is sure to wreak vengeance upon the foe who jeopardized the life of their vessel—even an evil entity won't change allegiances or ignore danger except in the most extreme circumstances.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the living vessel archetype.

<title level="2">Living Vessel Dedication leads to...</title>
[Entity's Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=3816), [Exude Abyssal Corruption](/Feats.aspx?ID=3818), [Fey's Trickery](/Feats.aspx?ID=3819), [Tap Vitality](/Feats.aspx?ID=3817), [Vessel's Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=3821), [Warped Constriction](/Feats.aspx?ID=3820)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fleshwarp" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=338" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 92

</column>

---

You've learned to use part of your form as a weapon. When you select this feat, you gain a claws unarmed attack that deals 1d4 slashing damage and has the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170) and [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179) traits; a horn, jaws, or tusk unarmed attack that deals 1d6 piercing damage and has the [versatile S](/Traits.aspx?ID=200) trait; or a tail unarmed attack that deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage and has the [backswing](/Traits.aspx?ID=173) trait. Each of these unarmed attacks is in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) weapon group. 

Your features are mutable; you can select this feat at any level, and you can retrain into or out of this feat or change the type of attack you gain.

**Special** You can take this feat multiple times. Each time you do, select a new attack from the options above.

During your daily preparations, you can gain the assistance of an allied prepared spellcaster to prepare one spell for the day. The spell can be up to 3rd level. Your ally must be able to prepare and cast it, and the spell must have a Targets entry or an area. Your ally loses a spell slot of the corresponding spell level, and you gain the ability to cast the prepared spell once that day. When you Cast the Spell, use your class DC for any saving throws required by the spell, and your class DC – 10 as a spell attack roll modifier.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />
<trait label="Guardian" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=859" />

---

You attack an enemy to ensure they can't move beyond your reach. Strike an enemy within your reach. If you hit and deal  damage, that enemy can't use move actions to move beyond the reach of the weapon or unarmed attack you used for the  Strike. The enemy can still move to other squares within reach of that weapon or unarmed attack. This effect lasts until the beginning of your next turn, until you move, or until you use that weapon or unarmed attack to make another attack, whichever comes first.

**Prerequisites**
[construct innovation](/Innovations.aspx?ID=2)

</column>

---

Aha! You lock on to your enemy's weak point to assist your construct companion in destroying it. When you Lock On, designate an enemy you can see. If your next action is to Command your construct, the construct gains a +2 circumstance bonus to attack rolls against the designated enemy until the end of the turn. If you use 2 actions for the Command, the bonus is instead a +3 circumstance bonus, or a +4 circumstance bonus if you're legendary in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4).

    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Lonely Army](/Feats.aspx?ID=7940) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 61

**Archetype** [Guerrilla](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=327)

**Prerequisites**
[Guerrilla Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7931)

**Requirements**
You are in your favored location; you are currently [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79), unobserved, or unnoticed by all enemies; and you are not [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73).

</column>

---

You move and attack with deadly silence, unbelievable speed, and unlimited ferocity. Strike with a [blowgun](/Weapons.aspx?ID=424) or [sling](/Weapons.aspx?ID=430); if the Strike is successful, the enemy cannot tell where it came from and you remain hidden. Immediately after the successful Strike, you can [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405) to a new location, Interact to reload a blowgun or sling, and Strike again, remaining hidden on a successful Strike. If the second Strike is successful, you can Sneak, Interact to reload, and then Strike with a sling or blowgun a third time, remaining hidden after a  successful Strike.  

After using Lonely Army, you are fatigued for 1 minute.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Long-Nosed Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=1316) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=127" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Tengu" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=240" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 26

</column>

---

You can transform into a specific, curious-looking human form. This human form is the same age and body type as your tengu form and has roughly analogous physical traits, such as height, though your nose remains as long as your beak and your complexion has red undertones, no matter the skin color of your human form. Using Long-Nosed Form counts as creating a disguise for the [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) use of [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5). Due to your imperfect transformation, your transformation doesn't automatically defeat Perception DCs to determine whether you are human, though you may be able to explain away or hide your tengu traits. You lose your beak unarmed Strike in your human form, as well as any other unarmed Strikes you gained from a tengu heritage or ancestry feat. You can remain in your human form indefinitely, and you can shift back to your tengu form by using this action again.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=812" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 199

**Requirements**
You’re adjacent to an enemy larger than you.

</column>

---

Using a technique pioneered by goblins, you conceal your movements from a larger creature and hit them where it hurts. You use Quick Alchemy to create a bomb or quick vial, then Strike an adjacent creature that’s larger than you with it; neither action triggers reactions from the target of your Strike. The creature is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to your Strike, but the bomb doesn’t deal its [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) damage.

**Special** If you have the Quick Bomber feat, you can [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304) after making the Strike, though you must remain adjacent to the required creature.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Captivator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3358)

</column>

---

If your [illusions](/Traits.aspx?ID=92) or [enchantments](/Traits.aspx?ID=61) fail to ensnare the minds of others, you can cast them again. If your next action is to cast an innate enchantment or illusion spell and it fails to affect any targets, you do not lose the spell. You must use the same number of actions to recast the same spell on your following turn; if you can't, or choose not to, you waste that number of actions with no effect. After this second casting, you lose the spell whether it affected any targets or not. Look Again works only with spells that require targets and doesn't do anything if you cast a targeted spell but didn't select any targets.

You are trained in [Loremaster Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8), a special Lore skill that can be used only to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26), but on any topic. If you have legendary proficiency in a skill used to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=22), you gain expert proficiency in Loremaster Lore, but you can't increase your proficiency rank in Loremaster Lore by any other means. You can take feats in the loremaster's additional feats entry even if you don't meet the enigma muse prerequisite. 

If you have the [Bardic Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=179) class feat, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to skill checks with Bardic Lore.

Your enemy lies in wait, lines up the perfect shot, and pulls the trigger... then at just the right moment you duck down to notice something scrawled on the cobblestone in chalk, a shiny coin, or some other coincidental distraction, creating an opportunity for the attack to miss. The attacker must roll the attack twice and use the worse result.

</title>

<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />

Through your wiles, charm, or a little bit of magic, you lure in a foe for a closer look—and a quick bite! Choose a creature within 30 feet. It must attempt a Will save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. If the target fails its save, you pull it up to 30 feet. If the target ends this movement in reach of your jaws, you can attempt a jaws Strike against it. Regardless of the result of its save, the target is temporarily immune for 24 hours.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Macabre Virtuoso](/Feats.aspx?ID=3488) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 34

**Archetype** [Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=175)

**Prerequisites**
[Reanimator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3486); Expert in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), Expert in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or Expert in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

</column>

---

Any necromancer can create [zombie](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=103) and [skeleton](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=92), but you know the secrets behind the creation of far more advanced undead monstrosities. You learn the [_create undead_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=10) rituals to create two types of common [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) for which you meet the prerequisites. (Your GM might give you access to additional types of undead.) You can't teach these rituals to anyone else and you can't participate in either ritual while allowing someone else to serve as the primary caster unless they also know the ritual. When you reach a new level, you can change either or both of these rituals to a different type of undead for which you now meet the prerequisites.

 When acting as primary caster, you can perform all _create undead_ rituals in 4 hours instead of 1 day and you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your primary check. You can also perform the ritual without the aid of a secondary caster, in which case you attempt the secondary check.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time, you learn the rituals to create two more types of undead creatures.

fields.text: Feat 6 Macabre Virtuoso Uncommon Archetype Source Book of the Dead pg. 34 Archetype Reanimator Prerequisites Reanimator Dedication; Expert in Arcana, Expert in Occultism, or Expert in Religion Any necromancer can create zombie and skeleton, but you know the secrets behind the creation of far more advanced undead monstrosities. You learn the create undead rituals to create two types of common undead for which you meet the prerequisites. (Your GM might give you access to additional types of undead.) You can't teach these rituals to anyone else and you can't participate in either ritual while allowing someone else to serve as the primary caster unless they also know the ritual. When you reach a new level, you can change either or both of these rituals to a different type of undead for which you now meet the prerequisites. When acting as primary caster, you can perform all create undead rituals in 4 hours instead of 1 day and you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your primary check. You can also perform the ritual without the aid of a secondary caster, in which case you attempt the secondary check. Special You can select this feat more than once. Each time, you learn the rituals to create two more types of undead creatures.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Maelstrom Flow](/Feats.aspx?ID=7471) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 83

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
[Resurgent Maelstrom Hybrid Study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=9)

**Requirements**
You’re wielding an improvised weapon.

</column>

---

You pour energy into an improvised weapon, speeding its destruction to grant it power. The overloaded energy grants your improvised weapon the effect of the _[astral](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2832)_, _[corrosive](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2834)_, _[extending](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2836)_, or _[frost](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2839)_ rune for 1 minute, after which the item is destroyed. If the item has a Hardness greater than your level, or if it's an artifact, cursed item, or other item that's difficult to break or destroy, it is not destroyed, and this ability only lasts until the end of your turn.

This effect doesn't count against the number of property runes a weapon can have based on its potency rune, but a given weapon can only have one application of Maelstrom Flow at a time.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 101

**Archetype** [Magaambyan Attendant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=29)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) or Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10); member of the Magaambya of attendant rank

**Access**
A character who is Magaambyan of at least attendant rank has access to this option.

</column>

---

You devote much of your study to halcyon magic. You gain the ability to cast a single [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1) or [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4) cantrip of your choice, (as is normal for cantrips, it is heightened to a spell level equal to half your level, rounded up). If you weren’t already, you become trained in that tradition’s spell DCs and spell attack rolls, with Intelligence as your spellcasting ability if you choose arcane or Wisdom as your spellcasting ability if you choose primal.

 Regardless of whether you choose an arcane or primal cantrip, you also either become trained in Arcana or Nature, or an expert in one of those skills in which you were already trained.

 When you gain this feat, choose to affiliate with the Cascade Bearers, Emerald Boughs, Rain–Scribes, Tempest-Sun Mages, or Uzunjati. This grants you additional feats available to only that branch.

**Special** You cannot select another dedication feat other than [Halcyon Speaker Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1115) until you have gained two other feats from the Magaambyan Attendant or [halcyon speaker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=30) archetype.

<title level="2">Magaambyan Attendant Dedication leads to...</title>
[Cascade Bearer's Flexibility](/Feats.aspx?ID=1105), [Cascade Bearer's Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=1110), [Emerald Boughs Accustomation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1106), [Emerald Boughs Hideaway](/Feats.aspx?ID=1111), [Faith in the Fallen](/Feats.aspx?ID=7759), [Halcyon Speaker Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1115), [Mask Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=1103), [Rain-Scribe Mobility](/Feats.aspx?ID=1112), [Rain-Scribe Sustenance](/Feats.aspx?ID=1107), [Tempest-Sun Redirection](/Feats.aspx?ID=1108), [Uzunjati Storytelling](/Feats.aspx?ID=1109)
